name: Tulsa
industrialProfile: Tulsa runs two industrial economies at once. HF Sinclair's Tulsa East and West plants, bought from Sinclair and Sunoco in 2009, process 125,000 barrels a day, while ONEOK and Williams run their gathering, NGL and Transco pipeline networks from downtown towers. Across town, American Airlines' 3.3-million-square-foot Tulsa Maintenance Base is the largest commercial aircraft maintenance operation in the world, overhauling roughly 80% of the fleet with over 5,000 mechanics; Spirit AeroSystems builds Boeing structures inside former Air Force Plant No. 3, and NORDAM repairs nacelles and thrust reversers. Barge traffic terminates at the Port of Catoosa.
localCompliance: NAS 410 and FAA 14 CFR Part 145 repair station requirements
ASME BPVC Section VIII Div 1 and NBIC NB-23

name: Huntsville
industries: Rocket propulsion and launch vehicle manufacturing
industrialProfile: Huntsville's inspection demand is propulsion and nuclear, not process. Blue Origin's 600,000-square-foot Blue Engine plant builds BE-4 and BE-3U engines at high rate; NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center on Redstone Arsenal owns Space Launch System development; and west in Decatur, United Launch Alliance's 1.6-million-square-foot factory assembles Vulcan Centaur and barges it down the Tennessee River. TVA's Browns Ferry plant, 28 miles out in Limestone County, runs three GE boiling-water reactors at 3,775 MWe. Mazda Toyota Manufacturing USA and Nucor Steel Decatur add automotive and steel volume alongside the aerospace work.

name: Denver
industries: DJ Basin oil and gas midstream
companies: BAE Systems Space & Mission Systems (formerly Ball Aerospace)
industrialProfile: Denver pairs a single refinery with the densest space-hardware cluster in the Rockies. Suncor's Commerce City refinery is Colorado's only one, 98,000 barrels a day of gasoline, diesel and paving asphalt, and a 2024 $10.5 million state settlement, the largest ever against one Colorado facility, keeps its mechanical integrity under real scrutiny. Lockheed Martin Space is headquartered in Littleton building Orion; BAE Systems Space & Mission Systems, the former Ball Aerospace, occupies Boulder, Broomfield and Westminster; United Launch Alliance runs program management from Centennial. Vestas assembles nacelles in Brighton, and Molson Coors' Golden site is the world's largest single-site brewery.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section VIII Div 1 and NBIC NB-23

name: Colorado Springs
industries: Custom pressure vessel and skid fabrication
companies: Peterson Space Force Base and Cheyenne Mountain Space Force Station
industrialProfile: Colorado Springs is a defense town with a small, code-stamped fabrication tail. Military installations and contractors supply over 40% of the regional economy: Peterson Space Force Base hosts NORAD and U.S. Northern Command, with Schriever, Cheyenne Mountain Space Force Station, Fort Carson and the Air Force Academy nearby and roughly 45,000 active-duty troops. Northrop Grumman, Boeing, L3Harris, General Dynamics and SAIC staff the programs. Manufacturing is narrower: Microchip Technology runs the former Atmel wafer fab, Keysight does oscilloscope R&D, and Springs Fabrication on Aeroplaza Drive holds an ASME U Certificate and ITAR registration for pressure vessels, vacuum chambers and launch ground-support equipment.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section VIII Div 1 (U Certificate of Authorization)

name: Deer Park
industries: Bulk liquid terminals and tank storage
companies: Dow Deer Park (former Rohm and Haas)
industrialProfile: Deer Park packs a refinery and four major chemical complexes into ten square miles between the Houston Ship Channel and State Highway 225. Pemex took full ownership of the former Shell refinery in January 2022 and runs it with about 1,500 people; Shell kept the 1,200-acre chemical plant next door at similar headcount. Dow's site, the old Rohm and Haas works, covers 900 acres; Lubrizol's specialty chemicals operation spans over 330 acres with roughly 1,000 employees; and Intercontinental Terminals' tank farm burned for days in March 2019. Fixed equipment, tank bottoms and turnaround crews are the standing workload.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section VIII and NBIC NB-23

name: Sugar Land
industries: EPC engineering for refining and petrochemicals
industrialProfile: Sugar Land's industrial base is technical rather than smokestack. The sugar refinery it was named for closed in 2003, though Imperial Sugar kept its headquarters. SLB moved its U.S. corporate headquarters onto a 33-acre campus at U.S. 90A and Gillingham Lane in 2015 and is among the city's largest employers. Fluor Enterprises runs about 1,980 people doing EPC design for refining and petrochemical projects built elsewhere on the Gulf Coast; Nalco Champion formulates production chemicals with roughly 1,216. Team, Inc., a national NDT and mechanical services contractor, is headquartered on Dairy Ashford Road. Work here is specification, procedure qualification and vendor surveillance.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section V and Section VIII

name: Lima
companies: Joint Systems Manufacturing Center (General Dynamics Land Systems)
industrialProfile: Lima is an Allen County city of about 35,000 carrying an outsized heavy-industrial load. Cenovus's Lima Refinery traces to Solar Refining in 1886 and passed through Standard Oil of Ohio, BP, Clark, Premcor, Valero and Husky; a 2019 project let it run heavy crude alongside light, making low-sulfur gasoline, ULSD, jet fuel and petrochemical feedstock for five states. The Joint Systems Manufacturing Center, still called the Lima Army Tank Plant, is government-owned and operated by General Dynamics Land Systems as the country's only M1 Abrams line. Ford's Lima Engine plant builds EcoBoost and Duratec V6s; INEOS Nitriles makes 190,000 tonnes of acrylonitrile plus HCN.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section VIII Div 1 and NBIC NB-23

name: Chicago
companies: Cleveland-Cliffs Burns Harbor and Indiana Harbor
industrialProfile: Chicago's inspection demand sits in a ring around the city rather than inside it. BP's Whiting refinery runs more than 400,000 bpd across Whiting, Hammond and East Chicago, and CITGO's Lemont refinery at Romeoville adds 183,000 bpd on the Sanitary and Ship Canal. The Calumet corridor still carries U.S. Steel's Gary Works, North America's largest integrated mill at 8.2 million tons, plus Cleveland-Cliffs at Burns Harbor and Indiana Harbor. Constellation's Dresden station near Morris sits 43 miles out. Add the nation's railroad hub, and one crew may cover refinery turnarounds, coke batteries, plate mills and tank cars in a single week.
localCompliance: ASME Section VIII Div. 1 and NBIC NB-23 repair/alteration
10 CFR 50 Appendix B and ASME Section XI (Constellation fleet)

name: Los Angeles
industrialProfile: Los Angeles pairs refining with aerospace inside the same few ZIP codes. Chevron's El Segundo refinery runs 276,000 bpd and covers more than a quarter of that city's land area; Marathon's Los Angeles refinery straddles Carson and Wilmington, where roughly 20 percent of the land is refinery. A few blocks inland, El Segundo holds Boeing's Satellite Development Center, Raytheon, Northrop Grumman and The Aerospace Corporation, over 20,000 aerospace jobs in one small city. Wilmington and San Pedro form the Port of Los Angeles waterfront. The result is refinery turnaround work under California's refinery-specific PSM rule and Nadcap-audited aerospace NDT within the same commute.
localCompliance: Cal/OSHA Process Safety Management for Petroleum Refineries (8 CCR 5189.1)
ASTM E1417 / E1444 penetrant and magnetic particle
AWS D1.1 and D1.8 seismic supplement

name: Pittsburgh
companies: U.S. Steel Mon Valley Works (Edgar Thomson, Irvin, Clairton Coke Works)
Beaver Valley Power Station (Vistra, Shippingport, PA)
industrialProfile: Pittsburgh stacks steel, shale gas and nuclear into the same river valleys. U.S. Steel's Mon Valley Works, Edgar Thomson at Braddock, the Irvin plant and Clairton Coke Works, remains the anchor, now under Nippon Steel with fresh investment announced for Edgar Thomson. Twenty-five miles down the Ohio, Shell's Monaca cracker converts Marcellus ethane into 1.6 million tons a year of polyethylene, and Vistra's two Beaver Valley PWRs sit 27 miles northwest at Shippingport. Westinghouse runs AP1000 engineering and plant services from Cranberry Township, EQT produces Appalachian gas from downtown, and Wabtec builds locomotives. Few metros mix Section XI, B31.8 and coke-battery work this tightly.
localCompliance: 10 CFR 50 Appendix B and ASME Section XI (Beaver Valley, Westinghouse supply chain)
49 CFR 192 and PA Act 127 (gas gathering and transmission)
ASME Section VIII and NBIC NB-23
AMS-STD-2154 ultrasonic inspection of wrought metals

name: New Orleans
companies: NASA Michoud Assembly Facility (Boeing SLS core stage, Lockheed Martin Orion)
industrialProfile: New Orleans inspection work follows the river and the marsh. PBF's Chalmette Refining runs 185,000 bpd on the Mississippi in St. Bernard Parish; the Shell/Valero complex at Norco sits upriver, and Entergy's Waterford 3 PWR is at Killona, 25 miles west. NASA's Michoud Assembly Facility in New Orleans East holds 43 acres of climate-controlled floor where Boeing fabricates SLS core stages and Lockheed Martin welds Orion pressure vessels. Textron Marine & Land Systems builds Ship-to-Shore Connectors at Slidell, and Bollinger's Lockport and Houma yards turn out Coast Guard cutters and Navajo-class salvage ships. The Port of South Louisiana leads all US ports by tonnage.
localCompliance: OSHA PSM (29 CFR 1910.119) and EPA RMP
USCG Subchapter M and ABS Rules for Building and Classing Steel Vessels
AWS D17.1 and NASA-STD-5006 aerospace welding

name: Norfolk
industries: Naval shipbuilding and nuclear ship repair
Commercial ship repair and marine fabrication
industrialProfile: Hampton Roads is the densest ship-repair market in the country. Norfolk Naval Shipyard in Portsmouth is the Navy's oldest and largest industrial facility and one of the few East Coast yards able to dry-dock a nuclear carrier. Across the James, Huntington Ingalls' Newport News Shipbuilding spans 550 acres as the sole US builder and refueler of aircraft carriers and one of two submarine builders. Private repair adds BAE Systems Norfolk and Colonna's Shipyard in Berkley, family-owned since 1875. Dominion's two Surry PWRs sit 30 miles up the James, and regional coal piers load over 65 million tons a year. Roughly 45 percent of regional output is defense-related.
localCompliance: NAVSEA Standard Items (009-06 welding and NDT)
10 CFR 50 Appendix B and ASME Section XI (Surry, naval nuclear work)
ABS Rules for Steel Vessels and USCG Subchapter M

name: Mobile
companies: Airbus Final Assembly Line, Mobile Aeroplex at Brookley
industrialProfile: Mobile builds aluminium warships and Airbus jets off the same bay. Austal USA on Blakeley Island produced the Independence-class LCS and Spearhead-class EPF and holds a contract for up to eleven Offshore Patrol Cutters. At the Mobile Aeroplex at Brookley, Airbus assembles A319, A320 and A321 aircraft, adding A220 production in 2019. North of the city, AM/NS Calvert, the ArcelorMittal and Nippon Steel joint venture, and Outokumpu's stainless line run flat-rolled steel, while SSAB's Axis mini-mill makes 1.25 million tonnes of discrete and coiled plate a year. The Port of Mobile is Alabama's only deep-water port. Naval, aerospace and plate acceptance codes all land on one crew.
localCompliance: EN 4179 and NAS 410 NDT personnel qualification (Airbus programme)
ABS Rules for Steel Vessels and USCG Subchapter M
ASTM A578 / A435 ultrasonic examination of plate

name: Galveston
industrialProfile: Galveston is an island port with the refining belt ten miles across the causeway. Marathon's Galveston Bay refinery at Texas City is the second-largest in Texas and third-largest in the country, and the Port of Texas City moves over 78 million tons a year, eighth-busiest in the US. On the island itself, Gulf Copper's Todd Road yard does ship repair, fabrication and new construction, including Coast Guard Arctic Security Cutters. Pelican Island holds Texas A&M Maritime Academy, the only US maritime academy on the Gulf, training licensed deck and engineering officers aboard the TS Kennedy. Galveston is also North America's fourth-busiest cruise homeport.
localCompliance: ABS Rules for Steel Vessels and USCG Subchapter M
API RP 2X and AWS D1.1 (offshore structural welds)
NBIC NB-23 and Texas Boiler Law (TDLR)

name: Corpus Christi
industries: Crude oil and LNG export terminals
companies: Flint Hills Resources Corpus Christi West Refinery
Valero Corpus Christi East and West Refineries
Cheniere Corpus Christi LNG (La Quinta Ship Channel)
Corpus Christi Army Depot at NAS Corpus Christi
industrialProfile: Three refineries line the Corpus Christi Ship Channel: Flint Hills Resources Corpus Christi West at roughly 300,000 b/d, CITGO at about 157,000 b/d, and Valero's East and West plants at a combined 370,000 b/d, East on light sweet crude and West on heavier grades. Cheniere's three-train LNG terminal sits on the La Quinta Channel, with the ExxonMobil-SABIC Gulf Coast Growth Ventures cracker at Gregory and Chemours' refrigerant plant nearby. Enbridge Ingleside Energy Center, the largest US crude export terminal, loaded 415 million barrels in 2025. Corpus Christi Army Depot is the world's largest helicopter overhaul facility, and Kiewit Offshore Services' 550-acre Ingleside yard builds offshore jackets and topsides.
localCompliance: NAS 410 and FAA 14 CFR Part 145 (depot and aviation MRO)

name: Beaumont
companies: ExxonMobil Beaumont Chemical and Polyethylene Plants
OCI Beaumont methanol and ammonia plant
industrialProfile: ExxonMobil's Beaumont refinery absorbed a 250,000 b/d expansion in 2023, the largest US refinery expansion since 2012, lifting local processing 65 percent to over 630,000 b/d and anchoring an adjoining chemical plant, polyethylene plant and lubricant blending works on the Neches River. Natgasoline's Beaumont plant is the largest methanol facility in the United States at 1.8 million tonnes a year; OCI Beaumont adds 730,000 tonnes of methanol and 265,000 tonnes of anhydrous ammonia; and Goodyear's 4.3-million-square-foot Beaumont chemical plant makes polybutadiene, polyisoprene and solution SBR. The Port of Beaumont takes more military cargo tonnage than any other US port, with the Army's 842nd Transportation Battalion outloading armored brigade sets.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section VIII and ASME B31.3

name: Port Arthur
industries: Marine terminals on the Sabine-Neches Waterway
companies: TotalEnergies Port Arthur Refinery and steam cracker
industrialProfile: Port Arthur holds the largest crude refinery in North America, Motiva's 626,000 b/d plant, plus Valero Port Arthur at about 335,000 b/d and TotalEnergies at 225,000 b/d with an adjoining steam cracker, and Chevron Phillips Chemical's Port Arthur petrochemical site. Two LNG megaprojects sit on the same reach of the Sabine-Neches Waterway: ExxonMobil and QatarEnergy's Golden Pass terminal at Sabine Pass entering service, and Sempra's Port Arthur LNG, a joint venture with ConocoPhillips, with Trains 1 and 2 targeted for 2027 and 2028. Coker, hydrocracker, alkylation and cryogenic-piping inspection run simultaneously here with LNG construction weld volume.
localCompliance: ASME B31.3 and BPVC Section IX

name: Texas City
industrialProfile: Texas City is a single fencelined industrial complex on the west shore of Galveston Bay. Marathon's Galveston Bay Refinery, bought from BP in 2013 and merged with Marathon's former Texas City refinery in 2018, runs 585,000 b/d and is the city's largest employer with about 1,550 full-time staff plus thousands of rotating contractors; a reconfiguration completed in 2023 brought it to EPA Tier 3 gasoline sulfur limits. Valero's Texas City refinery and the Dow, INEOS and Eastman Chemical plants share the same complex, which forms the largest industrial tax base in Galveston County. Dock, jetty and tank work along the Texas City Ship Channel adds continuous storage-tank scope.

name: Baytown
companies: ExxonMobil Baytown Refinery and Olefins Plant
Chevron Phillips Chemical Cedar Bayou Plant
industrialProfile: Baytown couples ExxonMobil's integrated refinery, olefins plant and chemical works, one of the world's largest petroleum and petrochemical operations and home to a major ExxonMobil technology center, with Chevron Phillips Chemical's Cedar Bayou Plant, the company's largest US site at roughly 1,400 acres running seven process units for ethylene, propylene, normal alpha olefins, HDPE, LDPE, LLDPE and polyalphaolefins. Covestro's Baytown site on West Bay Road, operating since 1971, is its largest North American plant, making polyurethane and polycarbonate raw materials. JSW Steel USA rolls the widest steel plate in North America here, so plate ultrasonics and pipe-mill weld inspection run alongside cracker and hydroprocessing turnarounds.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section VIII and ASME B31.3

name: Freeport
industrialProfile: Freeport exists around Dow Texas Operations, Dow's largest integrated site at roughly 7,000 acres, which makes 44 percent of what Dow sells in the United States and over 21 percent of its global volume. BASF's Freeport site, its first manufacturing plant outside Europe when it opened in 1958, runs 26 plants with more than 850 employees and nearly as many contractors, while Olin operates over 200 miles of chlor-alkali pipeline in Brazoria County, most of it inside the Dow fenceline. Freeport LNG's three-train terminal on Quintana Island has exported since 2019. Port Freeport works the shortest deep-water channel on the Texas coast.
localCompliance: ASME B31.3 and BPVC Section VIII

name: La Porte
companies: LyondellBasell La Porte Complex (Equistar and Acetyls)
Dow La Porte and Dow Bayport (former Rohm and Haas)
Barbours Cut Container Terminal, Port Houston
industrialProfile: La Porte's Battleground Industrial District packs LyondellBasell's 540-acre La Porte Complex, bisected by Miller Cut-Off Road and combining Equistar's ethylene, propylene, LLDPE and LDPE units with the Acetyls manufacturing chain, against INEOS's 300-acre Battleground Manufacturing Complex, built in 1956 and now running seven polyethylene lines, a polypropylene line, a 20 MW cogeneration unit and a polyolefin technical center. Dow runs polymer chemicals on Independence Parkway South and the former Rohm and Haas Bayport plant on Bay Area Boulevard, and Kuraray America makes EVAL resins on Strang Road. Port Houston's Barbours Cut container terminal sits at the north end.
localCompliance: ASME B31.3 and BPVC Section VIII Div 1

name: Pasadena
companies: Chevron Phillips Chemical Pasadena Plastics Complex
industrialProfile: Pasadena, Texas runs from the Houston Ship Channel south into the Bayport Industrial District. Chevron's Pasadena Refinery, founded in 1920 and acquired from Petrobras, sits on the channel; Chevron Phillips Chemical's Pasadena Plastics Complex makes high-density polyethylene; and INEOS Phenol on Pasadena Freeway produces phenol and cumene, with a second INEOS site on Port Drive in Bayport. Goodyear's Bayport chemical plant occupies 55 acres between Pasadena and La Porte making hydroquinone, and LyondellBasell's Bayport Complex added an ethers unit converting TBA piped from Channelview into oxyfuels. Dense tank farms and barge docks make API 653 shell and floor work as routine as unit turnarounds.

name: Channelview
industrialProfile: Channelview is effectively one complex and the contractor cluster serving it. LyondellBasell's Channelview Complex covers about 4,000 acres on both sides of the ship channel roughly 20 miles east of downtown Houston, has operated since 1957 and carries around 2,000 employees and contractors. Channelview North's olefins units crack for ethylene, propylene, butadiene and benzene; Channelview South converts them into propylene oxide, styrene monomer, derivatives and gasoline blending components, and in 2023 started up one of the world's largest PO/TBA plants. Around it sit fabrication and maintenance firms such as Enpro Systems, Owens Specialty Company's 80,000-square-foot shop and Paton Engineers and Constructors.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section VIII Div 1 and Section IX

name: Sweeny
companies: Chevron Phillips Chemical Old Ocean complex
industrialProfile: Sweeny is a small Brazoria County town whose entire industrial base is one Phillips 66 site at neighbouring Old Ocean, about 65 miles southwest of Houston. The refinery, built in 1942 and acquired by Phillips in 1947, runs 265,000 b/d through crude and vacuum distillation, naphtha reforming, FCC, alkylation, hydrodesulfurization, aromatics units and a delayed coker. Bolted onto it, the Sweeny Hub's NGL fractionators have taken site fractionation capacity to 550,000 b/d across four trains. Chevron Phillips Chemical's co-located Old Ocean units make ethylene, propylene, 1-hexene and polyethylene. There is no second industry here: demand is turnarounds, cryogenic towers and the feed pipelines.
localCompliance: ASME B31.3 and BPVC Section VIII

name: Longview
industrialProfile: Longview's anchor is Eastman Chemical's Texas Operations at 300 Kodak Boulevard, about 6,000 acres with more than 200 buildings and roughly 1,490 employees, among the largest petrochemical sites in Texas, making intermediates for automotive interiors, food preservatives, cosmetics and personal care. Heavy fabrication is the other half of the base: Trinity Rail employs close to 1,000 people building railcars in Gregg County, Komatsu's Longview plant carries on the LeTourneau line of mining and drilling equipment, and AAON Coil Products added a 220,000-square-foot commercial HVAC building in 2019 on top of a plant it has run since 2000. Dana also manufactures locally.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section VIII Div 1 and Section IX

name: Tyler
industrialProfile: Tyler's inspection demand comes from three unlike sources rather than a petrochemical corridor. Delek US runs the Tyler refinery, an inland plant on East Texas crude and one of the four refineries in Delek's 302,000 b/d system alongside Big Spring, El Dorado and Krotz Springs. Tyler Pipe and Coupling, a McWane subsidiary, casts iron soil pipe, fittings and no-hub couplings for commercial drain, waste and vent plumbing, a foundry with its own radiographic and hydrostatic regime. Trane Technologies occupies more than 1.6 million square feet on 151 acres with about 2,600 employees building HVAC equipment, adding a 200,000-square-foot building in 2022.
localCompliance: ASTM A888 and CISPI 301 (cast iron soil pipe)

name: Midland
industrialProfile: Midland is the operational capital of the Midland Basin rather than a plant town: there is no refinery inside the city. Diamondback Energy is headquartered here, ExxonMobil concentrated its post-Pioneer Permian workforce in Midland and Big Lake after closing the $60 billion acquisition in May 2024, and Chevron, Apache, Occidental, Baker Hughes and SLB run district offices and service yards from the city. Inspection is upstream and midstream: wellhead and pressure-control equipment, drill pipe and OCTG, and Targa's WestTX system of 17 cryogenic processing plants and roughly 7,210 miles of gathering pipeline, most of it held in a joint venture across the Midland Basin.
localCompliance: API Spec 5CT and API RP 5A5 (OCTG and drill pipe inspection)
API Spec 6A and API 16A (wellhead and BOP equipment)
49 CFR 192 and 49 CFR 195 (gas and liquid pipelines)

name: Odessa
industries: Pressure vessel and production tank manufacturing
companies: 1PointFive STRATOS direct air capture plant, Ector County
industrialProfile: Odessa is the blue-collar half of the Permian. Saulsbury Industries is headquartered here and, with Halliburton and completion contractors, the top private employers exceed 6,000 people; mining, quarrying and oil and gas extraction is the single largest employment category at about 11,190 workers. The petrochemical era ended when Flint Hills Resources shut the former Rexene and Huntsman Odessa cracker and polyolefin units in 2008-09, with the site later taken by REXtac. What remains is code fabrication and service work, including Sivalls Inc. and Permian Tank & Manufacturing building separators, pressure vessels and production tanks. Occidental's 1PointFive STRATOS direct air capture plant is under construction near Penwell.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section VIII Div 1 and Section IX
API 12F and API 650 (production and welded storage tanks)
API Spec 5CT and API RP 5A5 (OCTG inspection)

name: San Antonio
companies: CPS Energy Calaveras Power Station (J.K. Spruce 1 and 2)
industrialProfile: San Antonio's inspection demand is aerospace sustainment and heavy assembly, not refining. Port San Antonio at Kelly Field hosts two of the world's largest aircraft sustainment operations: Boeing's Global Services San Antonio large-aircraft MRO, opened 1998, and StandardAero's 600,000-square-foot engine facility with indoor and outdoor test cells serving the Air Force, Navy, Coast Guard and DHS, on the region's longest runway at 11,500 feet. Toyota Motor Manufacturing Texas builds full-size trucks here and International Motors is investing $250 million in a new I-35 plant. CPS Energy runs J.K. Spruce 1 and 2 above 1,300 MW at Calaveras Lake and holds a 40 percent share of the South Texas Project.
localCompliance: 10 CFR 50 Appendix B (CPS Energy South Texas Project share)
ASME BPVC Section I and NBIC NB-23 (utility boilers)

name: Austin
companies: NXP Semiconductors Austin (Oak Hill and Ed Bluestein)
Austin Energy Sand Hill Energy Center and Decker Creek
industrialProfile: Austin's heavy industry is fabs and vehicle assembly. Samsung Austin Semiconductor runs its long-established Austin fab while the $17 billion Taylor plant to the northeast, the largest single foreign investment in Texas, ramps toward production. NXP operates two Austin campuses, Oak Hill and Ed Bluestein, with more than 2,700 employees on 200 mm automotive microcontrollers, a base now in transition as the company shifts toward 300 mm. Tesla assembles vehicles at Giga Texas in Del Valle. Austin Energy generates at the Sand Hill Energy Center and Decker Creek in east Austin, co-owns the Fayette Power Project with LCRA and holds a 16 percent share of the South Texas Project.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section IX (welding procedure and performance qualification)
10 CFR 50 Appendix B (Austin Energy South Texas Project share)

name: Laredo
companies: World Trade International Bridge, City of Laredo
CPKC Patrick J. Ottensmeyer International Railway Bridge
Union Pacific Laredo International Railroad Bridge
industrialProfile: Laredo has almost no process industry: no refinery, no cracker, no mill. Its industrial base is the crossing itself. Port Laredo is the busiest US port of entry by trade value, at about $199.2 billion year to date and roughly 6.94 percent of all US trade, with some 14,000 commercial trucks a day moving over the World Trade Bridge and Colombia Solidarity Bridge. CPKC opened the second span of the Patrick J. Ottensmeyer International Railway Bridge in February 2025, doubling capacity at North America's busiest rail border crossing, while Union Pacific works the older Laredo International Railroad Bridge. Demand is bridge steel, rail and intermodal equipment, cargo tanks and cross-border gas pipelines.
localCompliance: 49 CFR 180 (cargo tank and tank car requalification)
23 CFR 650 Subpart C (National Bridge Inspection Standards)

name: Brownsville
companies: International Shipbreaking Limited (EMR), Port of Brownsville
Karpowership Brownsville shipyard (former Keppel AmFELS / Seatrium)
industrialProfile: Brownsville's industry is cut steel and new steel. The Port of Brownsville's three ship recycling yards take over 85 percent of US Navy and MARAD ship recycling work, with International Shipbreaking Limited, part of UK-based EMR, the largest; it received the carrier USS John F. Kennedy in February 2025 for dismantling. The shipyard begun by Marathon LeTourneau in the early 1970s and run for three decades by Keppel AmFELS, then Seatrium, passed to Karpowership in 2025 with a $3 billion floating-power-plant investment. NextDecade's Rio Grande LNG is under construction at the port, and SpaceX's Starbase at Boca Chica is adding an 83-acre port dock and a Cameron County gas pipeline.
localCompliance: ABS Rules for Building and Classing Marine Vessels
USCG 46 CFR and 33 CFR 154 (vessel and transfer facility inspection)
ASME BPVC Section VIII Div 1 and Section IX

name: Victoria
industrialProfile: Victoria sits inland at the centre of a ring of Calhoun and Victoria County chemical plants reached by the Victoria Barge Canal. INVISTA's Victoria plant makes nylon intermediates within the Victoria Plastics Complex alongside Equistar and LyondellBasell units. Southeast of town, Formosa Plastics' Point Comfort site is the company's largest in the United States, 1,800 acres with about 330 full-time employees and up to 3,500 contract workers. Dow's Seadrift Operations and INEOS Nitriles' Green Lake plant, which uses propylene ammoxidation to make acrylonitrile, acetonitrile, HCN and ACH and runs a terminal at the Port of Point Comfort, complete the cluster. Caterpillar builds excavators in Victoria itself.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section VIII Div 1 and Section IX

name: Carson
industries: Bulk fuel terminals and pipeline logistics
companies: Marathon Los Angeles Refinery (Carson crude site)
Kinder Morgan Carson crude and products terminal
industrialProfile: Carson is the crude-processing half of Marathon's Los Angeles Refinery, the largest refinery on the West Coast at roughly 365,000 barrels per calendar day, which Marathon merged with its Wilmington site into one operation in 2019. The 425-MW Watson Cogeneration Plant sits on 21.7 acres alongside it supplying refinery steam and power. Air Products runs a hydrogen plant on Alameda Street feeding refinery hydrotreaters by pipeline, and Kinder Morgan operates crude and product storage here. Phillips 66's 235-acre Carson site stopped refining in late 2025, so demand now splits between live FCC, coker and alkylation service and decommissioning across a 650-acre Carson-Wilmington footprint.
localCompliance: Cal/OSHA Process Safety Management for Refineries (8 CCR §5189.1)
ASME Section VIII Div 1 and B31.3

name: Wilmington
industries: Marine liquid-bulk terminals and Port of Los Angeles cargo
companies: Marathon Los Angeles Refinery (Wilmington upgrading site)
California Resources Corporation and Tidelands Oil Production (Wilmington Oil Field)
Port of Los Angeles liquid-bulk berths, Cerritos Channel
industrialProfile: Wilmington sits directly on top of the Wilmington Oil Field, the third-largest field in the contiguous United States, and carries three refinery footprints within a few square miles. Valero's Wilmington refinery runs roughly 85,000 to 135,000 b/d beside the Port of Los Angeles. Marathon's Wilmington site upgrades intermediates piped from its Carson crude units as one 365,000-bpcd operation. Phillips 66's 424-acre Wilmington plant stopped refining in late 2025 and is slated for industrial and recreational redevelopment. Tidelands Oil Production and California Resources still work about 1,550 active wells producing near 46,000 b/d, while marine loading arms and wharf piping line the Cerritos Channel.
localCompliance: Cal/OSHA Process Safety Management for Refineries (8 CCR §5189.1)

name: Torrance
industries: Aerospace turbine engine manufacturing and overhaul
industrialProfile: Torrance pairs a 166,000-b/d refinery with one of Southern California's densest aerospace supplier clusters. PBF's Torrance refinery occupies about 700 acres, carries a Nelson complexity of 13.8, and makes CARB gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, LPG, coke and sulfur. Two miles away at Zamperini Field, Robinson Helicopter builds, assembles and flight-tests every R22, R44 and R66 it ships. Honeywell's largest Southern California plant, on West 190th Street, builds and overhauls TPE331 and HTF7000 turbine engines; Moog makes flight controls and landing gear here; LISI Aerospace and Conesys supply fasteners and connectors. industrialProfile: Dearborn is the Rouge. Ford's Dearborn Truck Plant builds F-150s on the historic Rouge site alongside the Rouge Electric Vehicle Center, Dearborn Stamping, Dearborn Diversified Manufacturing and the Research and Engineering Center, with presses, body shops, paint ovens and the complex's own powerhouse and steam distribution. Immediately adjacent, Cleveland-Cliffs Dearborn Works idled its blast furnace, BOF steel shop and continuous casters from July 2025 with roughly 600 layoffs, while finishing and coating lines continued; Cliffs said in mid-2026 it was exploring relighting the furnace. Dearborn's fixed-equipment work is therefore weighted toward automotive utilities and steel finishing rather than ironmaking.
localCompliance: AWS D1.1 and D1.3 with IATF 16949
ASME Section VIII Div. 1 and NBIC NB-23
ASME B31.1 power and steam piping
ASME B30.2 and B30.16 crane and hoist inspection

name: Trenton
industries: Power plant decommissioning and brownfield redevelopment
companies: DTE Trenton Channel Energy Center (220 MW battery storage)
Retired DTE Trenton Channel coal plant site
industrialProfile: Trenton is a Downriver city in visible transition. Stellantis's Trenton Engine Complex still builds both Pentastar 3.6-litre V6 variants, Classic for the Ram 1500 Classic and Upgrade for the Pacifica, Wrangler and Gladiator, so engine-line machining, compressed air, coolant and utility systems are the steady inspection base. On the Detroit River, DTE retired the Trenton Channel coal plant and is completing a 220 MW Trenton Channel Energy Center on the site, the largest standalone battery storage project in the Great Lakes region, due in 2026. The McLouth Steel site next door is a cleared brownfield and BASF's Wyandotte North Works sits immediately upriver.
localCompliance: ASME Section VIII Div. 1 and NBIC NB-23
NFPA 855 and UL 9540A for battery energy storage installation and commissioning
ASME B31.3 process piping (Downriver chemical plants)

name: Cleveland
industries: Aerospace forgings and large structural forgings
Welding, fluid power and flow-control equipment
companies: Howmet Aerospace Cleveland Operations (50,000-ton forging press)
Ford Cleveland Engine Plant, Brook Park
Vistra Perry Nuclear Power Plant (North Perry, adjacent)
industrialProfile: Cleveland's inspection work concentrates in the Cuyahoga flats and the western aerospace corridor. Cleveland-Cliffs Cleveland Works is one of the most productive integrated mills in the world, and its No. 6 blast furnace was restarted through July 2025 as Dearborn's was idled. Howmet Aerospace's Cleveland Operations runs the 50,000-ton forging press, turning out large structural forgings where ultrasonic and penetrant acceptance criteria are contractual. Ford's Cleveland Engine Plant in Brook Park, Lincoln Electric in Euclid, Parker Hannifin and Swagelok fill out the manufacturing base, NASA Glenn adds propulsion and materials testing, and Vistra's 1,268 MW Perry BWR is 40 miles northeast on Lake Erie.
localCompliance: ASTM E1417 and E1444 penetrant and magnetic particle
ASTM A388 and AMS 2630 ultrasonic inspection of forgings
ASME Section VIII Div. 1 and NBIC NB-23
10 CFR 50 Appendix B and ASME Section XI (Perry)

name: Lorain
industries: Great Lakes port, harbour and river marine work
companies: Ford Ohio Assembly Plant, Avon Lake (adjacent)
Port of Lorain and Black River terminals
industrialProfile: Lorain's heavy-metals era has largely ended and the profile should say so: U.S. Steel permanently shut the Lorain Tubular seamless mill that once made 380,000 net tons a year of OCTG, casing and line pipe, Republic Steel's Lorain bar operations wound down, and the Avon Lake coal plant was retired and demolished. What drives inspection now is automotive. Ford's 3.7-million-square-foot Ohio Assembly Plant on 419 acres at Avon Lake, Sheffield Lake and Sheffield Village builds the E-Series, Super Duty and F-650/F-750 and is taking a $1.5 billion commercial-EV expansion. Camaco's Lorain seat-frame plant feeds it, and Black River harbour terminals sustain marine and structural steelwork.
localCompliance: AWS D1.1 and D1.3 with IATF 16949
ASME Section VIII Div. 1 and NBIC NB-23
ASME B30.2 and B30.16 crane and hoist inspection
USCG 46 CFR Subchapter F and ABS Great Lakes vessel rules

name: Middletown
industrialProfile: Middletown is a Cleveland-Cliffs town and the mill is fully integrated: coke ovens, blast furnace, basic oxygen furnaces, vacuum degassers, slab casters, hot and cold mills and galvanising and aluminising lines on Crawford Street, producing enamelling steels sold as UNIVIT and VIT-PLUS, aluminised sheet and ULTRALUME advanced high-strength grades for automotive, appliance, HVAC and culvert customers. SunCoke's Middletown Coke Company on Yankee Road feeds it heat-recovery coke and cogenerated power, and Air Products runs a cogeneration plant on Cincinnati-Dayton Road. Beyond the steel complex the list is short: Essity's tissue operation on Columbia Avenue and Weidmann Electrical Technology's transformer insulation plant on Charles Street.

name: Baton Rouge
industries: Mississippi River terminals and barge logistics
industrialProfile: ExxonMobil's Baton Rouge refinery anchors the metro at over 500,000 bpd, among the largest in the United States, and runs alongside the company's adjacent chemical, plastics and lubricants plants on Scenic Highway. Across the river, Placid Refining's Port Allen refinery processes roughly 75,000 bpd, while Georgia-Pacific's Port Hudson mill in Zachary makes Brawny and Quilted Northern on 1,350 acres with more than 850 workers. Baton Rouge is also the home office of the river corridor's turnaround contractors, Turner Industries and Cajun Industries, so inspection crews are dispatched from here to plants from Geismar down to Norco.
localCompliance: ASME Section VIII Div 1 and B31.3

name: Lake Charles
industries: Marine terminals and ship channel logistics
industrialProfile: Work here follows the Calcasieu Ship Channel. CITGO's Lake Charles Manufacturing Complex, a refinery plus lubricants plant on Highway 108, and the Phillips 66 refinery on 690 acres at Westlake handle the fuels side, while Sasol's Lake Charles Chemical Complex adds an ethane cracker, ethylene oxide and glycol units, Ziegler and Guerbet alcohols and alumina. The distinguishing load is LNG: Venture Global's Calcasieu Pass and Cameron LNG at Hackberry put cryogenic piping, API 620 tanks and nine percent nickel weld inspection alongside conventional refinery turnarounds, and new train construction keeps a rotating contract workforce in Calcasieu Parish year-round.

name: Geismar
industrialProfile: Geismar packs roughly twenty plants into a few square miles of east-bank Ascension Parish. BASF's site is the company's largest manufacturing facility in North America, about 32 production units and roughly 1,300 employees. Shell Chemical has held its 800-acre alpha-olefins site since 1967; a fourth AO unit added 425 kilotons a year and made it the world's largest single-site alpha-olefins producer. Methanex's G1, G2 and G3 plants total about 4 million tonnes of methanol annually, with G3 running since mid-2024. NOVA Chemicals' ethane cracker, bought from Williams for $2.1 billion, sits near 900,000 tonnes of ethylene. Honeywell makes fluorine products and HFO refrigerants; Nutrien makes nitrogen.

name: Norco
companies: Shell Energy and Chemicals Park Norco
industrialProfile: Norco takes its name from the New Orleans Refining Company, and Shell has been on the site since 1929. The complex is now Shell Energy and Chemicals Park Norco, the only Shell site of that kind in the United States, pairing a roughly 250,000 bpd refinery with a cracker making ethylene, propylene and butadiene. Immediately alongside sits Valero's St. Charles refinery, one of the newest large refineries in the country at about 300,000 bpd. Across the river at Killona, Entergy's Waterford 3 pressurized-water reactor adds ASME Section XI and 10 CFR 50 Appendix B work to a parish otherwise dominated by hydrocarbons.

name: Garyville
industries: Bulk marine terminals and coal export
industrialProfile: Garyville exists around one plant: Marathon's Garyville refinery, which came online in 1977 as the last large grassroots refinery built in the United States and now runs about 617,000 barrels per calendar day, third largest in the country, on the Mississippi's east bank in St. John the Baptist Parish. Six miles upriver at Gramercy, Atalco's Atlantic Alumina is the only major alumina refinery still operating in the US, with roughly 550 workers and a Defense Department-backed gallium expansion. Coal moves through SunCoke's Convent Marine Terminal and grain through Zen-Noh's export elevator nearby. Marathon's turnaround cycle sets the inspection calendar for the whole town.

name: Convent
industrialProfile: Convent is the seat of St. James Parish and its demand is unusually mixed for the river corridor. Nucor Steel Louisiana runs the world's largest HYL direct-reduced-iron plant here at 2.5 million tons a year, with ExxonMobil capturing CO2 from the site beginning in 2026. OxyChem's Convent plant makes chlorine, caustic soda and ethylene dichloride, and Mosaic's Uncle Sam complex nearby produces phosphate fertilizer and sulfuric acid behind a 200-foot gypsum stack. River terminals add dock and conveyor work: SunCoke's Convent Marine Terminal for coal and Zen-Noh's grain elevator on Highway 44. Shell's 4,400-acre Convent refinery has been shut since November 2020.

name: Westlake
industrialProfile: Westlake sits on the west bank of the Calcasieu River opposite Lake Charles and holds three of the region's biggest process plants. The Phillips 66 Lake Charles refinery covers about 690 acres with crude, FCC, alkylation, hydrocracking and delayed coking units. Sasol's Lake Charles Chemical Complex on Old Spanish Trail runs an ethane cracker plus ethylene oxide and glycol, Ziegler and Guerbet alcohol, ethoxylate and LDPE units. Lotte Chemical Louisiana operates its own cracker and monoethylene glycol plant, and Louisiana Pigment, a Kronos and Venator joint venture, makes over 168,000 tonnes of chloride-process titanium dioxide a year alongside Westlake's chlor-alkali and VCM assets.

name: Sulphur
companies: CITGO Lake Charles Manufacturing Complex (Highway 108 South)
Westlake Corporation Sulphur polyethylene and ethylene plants
industrialProfile: Sulphur is where much of the Calcasieu corridor's mailing addresses actually land. CITGO's Lake Charles refinery and lubricants plant sit at 4401 Highway 108 South in Sulphur. Westlake's ethylene, styrene and polyethylene units, operated since 1986 on South Cities Service Highway and ISCC PLUS certified in 2025, are a short distance away. Firestone Polymers has made synthetic rubber and latex on Highway 108 East since the plant opened around 1943, now under Bridgestone ownership. The town has no port of its own, so the work is fixed equipment: crackers, reactors, storage spheres, rail loading racks and the piping tying them into the ship channel plants.

name: Plaquemine
industrialProfile: Plaquemine is a west-bank Iberville Parish company town built around Dow's Louisiana Operations, opened in 1956, running 23 production units and more than 50 intermediate and specialty products, and the largest employer in both Iberville and West Baton Rouge parishes; the site's utilities, docks and rail now sit under Diamond Infrastructure Solutions. Shintech's Plaquemine complex carries roughly 2.95 million metric tons a year of VCM capacity and has announced a $3.4 billion expansion adding a 500,000 t/y ethane cracker, a chlor-alkali plant and downstream EDC and VCM units. Olin runs chlor-alkali on the same corridor, so chlorine, caustic and vinyl service dominate the inspection workload.

name: St. Rose
companies: Shell Energy and Chemicals Park Norco
industrialProfile: St. Rose is a tank-farm town rather than a refinery town. IMTT's St. Rose terminal, operating since the 1960s, spreads about 1,000 acres between the Mississippi and Interstate 10 with 220 tanks and close to 16 million barrels of storage, handling petroleum, commodity and specialty chemicals and vegetable and tropical oils across truck, rail, barge and LOOP pipeline connections. Entergy's Little Gypsy station at Montz adds 530 MW of gas generation beside the newer St. Charles Power Station, and St. Charles Clean Fuels has proposed a low-carbon ammonia plant on IMTT land. API 653 tank work, not unit turnarounds, is the staple here.

name: Chalmette
industrialProfile: St. Bernard Parish is a genuinely narrow base: two refineries and a sugar plant, with almost nothing else heavy. PBF Energy's Chalmette Refining on West St. Bernard Highway is a 185,000 b/d dual-train coking refinery with a Nelson complexity of 13.0, configured for both light and heavy crude, acquired from ExxonMobil and PDVSA in 2015. A few miles downriver at Meraux, Valero's 135,000 b/d refinery takes sour and sweet crude over its own dock and off the Louisiana Offshore Oil Port, moving gasoline, diesel, jet and high-sulphur fuel oil into Colonial Pipeline. ASR Group's Domino Sugar refinery at Arabi rounds it out. Demand here is turnaround fixed equipment: coke drums, crude and vacuum towers, exchanger bundles, dock piping and tankage.

name: Meraux
industries: Refinery marine docks and pipeline logistics
companies: Rain CII Carbon Chalmette calcining plant
industrialProfile: Meraux is a single-refinery community about fifteen miles down river from New Orleans. Valero's Meraux refinery, the former Murphy Oil plant, runs roughly 135,000 bpd through a 38,000 bpd fluid catalytic cracker, a 34,000 bpd hydrocracker, a 41,000 bpd high-pressure hydrotreater, a 12,000 bpd DAO hydrotreater and a 21,000 bpd ROSE solvent deasphalting unit, a heavy-crude configuration that makes hydrogen-service and high-temperature piping inspection routine. Crude arrives at the refinery dock via LOOP and product leaves on Colonial. Chalmette Refining and the Rain CII coke calciner are the next plants along the same stretch of river.

name: Shreveport
companies: Barksdale Air Force Base / Air Force Global Strike Command
industrialProfile: Calumet's Shreveport refinery runs about 60,000 bpd of paraffinic crude into base oils, waxes, solvents, asphalt and fuels, with capability for up to 25,000 bpd of sour crude — a specialty lubricants plant rather than a fuels refinery. At the Port of Caddo-Bossier, Benteler Steel/Tube operates a seamless and welded tube mill supporting roughly 675 jobs and has added a threading facility for hot-rolled seamless tube. Barksdale AFB hosts Air Force Global Strike Command headquarters and the 2nd Bomb Wing's B-52 fleet. Ternium USA, Pratt Industries and Glovis America occupy the port and the former GM assembly site. Haynesville Shale gathering and compression fill out the pipeline workload.

name: Lafayette
industrialProfile: Lafayette is Acadiana's oilfield service base rather than a processing city, with no refinery in the parish. SLB consolidated its North Gulf Coast divisions into a Lafayette operations hub, Halliburton and Baker Hughes run service bases across Lafayette, Broussard and New Iberia, and Expro, Oceaneering, Fugro and Superior Energy keep yards along the Highway 90 corridor toward the Port of Iberia. PHI Aviation is headquartered here and maintains its offshore helicopter fleet at Lafayette Regional. Stuller, the largest jewelry manufacturer in North America, employs more than 1,500 in precision production. The work is drill string, BOP, riser and pressure-equipment recertification between offshore hitches.

name: Houma
industrialProfile: Houma's yards line the Houma Navigation Canal. Bollinger Houma, the 437-acre former Gulf Island shipyard it acquired in 2021 with four floating drydocks, builds the Navy's T-ATS towing, salvage and rescue ships and the Regional Class Research Vessels for the National Science Foundation. Gulf Island Fabrication still runs its Houma facility for fabrication and services work. Danos, family-owned since 1947, operates its corporate headquarters and manufacturing at Gray just outside town after a purpose-built expansion. Terrebonne Parish work is hull plate and weld inspection, module and jacket fabrication, and crane and lifting-gear certification for boats working the Gulf.
localCompliance: ABS Rules for Building and Classing Steel Vessels

name: Morgan City
industrialProfile: Morgan City sits where the Atchafalaya meets the Intracoastal Waterway, and the offshore industry was launched from here in 1947 with the first well drilled out of sight of land. Conrad Shipyard keeps its original 12-acre Morgan City yard plus a 16-acre yard at Amelia building steel and aluminum tugs, towboats, barges, ferries and Navy YRBM berthing barges. Bollinger's Amelia yard covers 50 acres and a mile of waterfront doing liftboat, barge and vessel repair, and Swiftships builds and refits aluminum craft. St. Mary Parish demand is drydock hull survey, new-construction weld inspection and liftboat leg and jacking-system checks.

name: Pascagoula
industrialProfile: Pascagoula packs a major shipyard and a top-tier refinery onto one stretch of Mississippi Sound waterfront. HII's Ingalls Shipbuilding, the state's largest manufacturing employer with more than 11,000 workers, builds DDG-51 Flight III destroyers, LPD Flight II and LHA amphibious ships, modernises Zumwalt-class hulls, and won the Navy's FF(X) frigate design-and-build selection in December 2025. Chevron's Pascagoula Refinery runs 20 major process units, roughly 200 storage tanks and four marine terminals with seven berths, with a permitted expansion toward 394,000 b/d. Chevron Phillips Chemical operates a benzene unit on 3,000-plus adjacent acres. Bollinger Mississippi Shipbuilding, the former VT Halter yard, works 378 acres with a 225-metre tilt-beam launch for hulls to 50,000 dwt.

name: Gulfport
industrialProfile: Gulfport itself is light on heavy process industry, with its economy resting on the port, the military, healthcare and gaming rather than refining or petrochemicals. The Port of Gulfport works 250 acres and 6,000 feet of berthing with refrigerated cargo, and the 1,100-acre Naval Construction Battalion Center is the Atlantic Fleet's Seabee homeport. Mississippi Power's Plant Jack Watson on the Biloxi River has burned gas since its 2015 conversion from coal. The nearest heavy plant is Chemours' 2,600-acre DeLisle titanium dioxide works near Pass Christian, roughly 600 employees, where PCC Group plans a chlor-alkali unit. Ingalls is thirty miles east.

name: Theodore
companies: High-Purity Silicon America Corporation (former Mitsubishi Polysilicon)
Theodore Industrial Canal / Alabama State Port Authority
industrialProfile: Theodore is an industrial park built around a dredged canal off Mobile Bay, part of the MAST corridor of McIntosh, Axis, Saraland and Theodore that holds more than twenty-five chemical manufacturers. Evonik has produced here for over fifty years, making hydrogen peroxide used as a bleaching agent in pulp and paper along with silica products. High-Purity Silicon America, the former Mitsubishi Polysilicon, runs one of fewer than ten polycrystalline silicon plants in the world at roughly five percent of global output with about 150 employees, buying feedstock from Evonik next door and selling a byproduct back. Airgas operates here too, and the canal gives every tenant barge access.

name: Port Harcourt
industries: Marine fabrication and supply base logistics
companies: Indorama Eleme Petrochemicals and Fertilizer, Eleme
Onne Oil and Gas Free Zone operators
industrialProfile: Port Harcourt anchors Nigeria's Niger Delta oil province. NNPC's Port Harcourt Refining Company holds 210,000 bpd across two plants, a 150,000 bpd new refinery and a 60,000 bpd old unit, but has run only intermittently, shutting again in May 2025 with NNPC reviewing rehabilitation options alongside Chinese partners in 2026. Steadier inspection demand sits at Indorama Eleme Petrochemicals in Eleme, whose urea capacity is moving from 2.8 to 4.2 million tonnes a year on Line 3, and at Nigeria LNG on Bonny Island, where six trains make 22 MTPA and Train 7 passed 93% completion in mid-2026. Onne's Oil and Gas Free Zone supplies base, fabrication and subsea work for SPDC and offshore operators.

name: Lagos
companies: Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals, Lekki
industrialProfile: Lagos's inspection load is dominated by one asset. The Dangote Petroleum Refinery in the Lekki Free Trade Zone reached its full 650,000 bpd nameplate in February 2026 on a 6,180-acre site fed by roughly 1,100 km of subsea crude pipeline, with polypropylene and fertiliser units alongside and an announced expansion toward 1.4 million bpd. Marine work centres on Nigerdock's Snake Island yard, a fabrication and drydocking base now tied to a 45-year MSC container terminal concession, and on Lekki Deep Sea Port, operational since April 2023. Power-side inspection comes from Egbin at Ikorodu, Nigeria's largest thermal station at 1,320 MW across six 220 MW units.

name: South Africa
industries: Synthetic fuels and crude oil refining
industrialProfile: South Africa's refining base has contracted hard. Only three fuel producers still run: Astron Energy's 100,000 bpd Cape Town refinery, Natref at Sasolburg, the country's only inland crude refinery, commissioned in 1971, and Sasol's Secunda Synfuels complex, the world's largest commercial coal-to-liquids plant at roughly 150,000 bpd from 80 Sasol-Lurgi fixed-bed gasifiers. Sapref in Durban, at 180,000 bpd the country's biggest, has been shut since 2022 and Engen Durban since a 2020 fire, leaving about 260,000 bpd idle and under restart study by the Central Energy Fund. Eskom adds Koeberg's two roughly 970 MW PWRs, relicensed to 2044 and 2045, plus the Kusile and Medupi coal units.

name: Johannesburg
industries: Inland fuel refining and product pipelines
industrialProfile: Johannesburg's inspection market is inland heavy industry, not offshore. Rand Refinery at Germiston, established in 1920 to refine South African mine gold locally instead of in London, is the world's largest integrated single-site precious metals refining and smelting complex, so furnace, pressure and gas-line work runs there continuously. Sixty kilometres south, ArcelorMittal's Vanderbijlpark Works, one of the world's largest inland steel mills, anchors the Vaal Triangle alongside Sasol's Sasolburg operations and Natref, the country's only inland crude refinery, about 80 km from the city. Transnet's multi-product pipeline from Durban feeds the Gauteng terminals, and Witwatersrand mining houses drive shaft, headgear and process-plant inspection.

name: Cape Town
industries: Ship repair, drydocking and marine engineering
companies: Astron Energy Cape Town Refinery, Milnerton
Transnet National Ports Authority, Sturrock Dry Dock
Port of Cape Town ship repair contractors
industrialProfile: Cape Town's NDT demand splits three ways. Astron Energy's Milnerton refinery, at 100,000 bpd South Africa's third largest and one of only three fuel plants still running nationally, drives fixed-equipment and turnaround inspection. Thirty kilometres north at Melkbosstrand, Eskom's Koeberg operates two roughly 970 MW pressurised water reactors relicensed to July 2044 and November 2045 after steam generator replacement on both units, work carried out under National Nuclear Regulator oversight. In the port, Damen Shipyards Cape Town, with drydock capacity to 350 m, and the 359 m by 45 m Sturrock dry dock handle panamax vessels, offshore support ships and bulkers, with the city pushing to expand ship repair capacity.

name: Guyana
companies: Vreed-en-Hoop Shore Base Inc (NRG Holdings / Jan De Nul)
Guyana Power and Light / Wales Gas-to-Energy
industrialProfile: Guyana's industrial base is barely a decade old and almost entirely offshore. Four FPSOs work the Stabroek Block, Liza Destiny at about 130,000 bpd, Liza Unity and Prosperity at roughly 265,000 bpd each and One Guyana on Yellowtail at about 260,000 bpd, together producing around 900,000 bpd in Q2 2026. The fifth vessel, Errea Wittu, arrived on 21 August 2026 for Uaru start-up in Q4. Onshore work is shore-base and pipeline: the US$300 million Vreed-en-Hoop SURF base opened in January 2025, and the 300 MW Wales gas-to-energy plant with its NGL facility and roughly 250 km pipeline is chasing first power at end-2026. Beyond oil, only Bosai's Linden bauxite plant and the Aurora gold mine carry real fixed-plant inspection.

Local Content Act 2021 requirements for Guyanese-registered service providers

name: Aberdeen
industries: North Sea oil and gas production
industrialProfile: Aberdeen runs the UK Continental Shelf from onshore. The merger of TotalEnergies' UK upstream business with NEO NEXT completed on 30 March 2026, creating NEO NEXT+ (TotalEnergies 47.5%, HitecVision 28.875%, Repsol UK 23.625%), the largest independent UKCS producer at over 250,000 boe/d, holding Elgin/Franklin, Culzean, Shearwater, Alwyn North, Dunbar, Mariner and Penguins. Harbour Energy and Aberdeen-headquartered Ithaca Energy operate much of the rest, with Wood and Petrofac supplying life-of-field and late-life services. North of the city, the St Fergus terminal complex takes between 25% and 50% of UK gas through the SEGAL, SAGE and FUKA systems. The £420 million South Harbour and the 250-hectare Energy Transition Zone pull decommissioning and offshore wind into the same supply chain.

name: Stavanger
industrialProfile: Stavanger is Norway's operational base for the Norwegian Continental Shelf. Johan Sverdrup, 160 km west on the Utsira High in 110 to 120 m of water, is run from here and produces 720,000 to 755,000 boe/d, its rich gas routed by Statpipe to the Kårstø plant in Rogaland, which handles around 98 million standard cubic metres of rich gas and is planning a membrane CO2 removal unit for about 2029. ConocoPhillips operates the Greater Ekofisk area some 300 km southwest, with Aker Solutions running Eldfisk and Ekofisk maintenance and modification from its Stavanger office and Egersund yard. Worley Rosenberg's Stavanger yard holds a five-year Equinor framework from May 2026 plus Fram Sør subsea fabrication.

name: Rotterdam
companies: Shell Energy and Chemicals Park Rotterdam (Pernis)
industrialProfile: Rotterdam holds Europe's largest refining and petrochemical cluster. Shell's Energy and Chemicals Park at Pernis runs around 400,000 bpd and is being tied to a 32 km hydrogen pipeline from a 200 MW electrolyser on Maasvlakte. BP's Europoort refinery, wholly BP-owned since the Nerefco buyout and covering roughly 390 hectares, is one of only two BP sites at or above 400,000 bpd, and ExxonMobil's Rotterdam refinery runs 191,000 bpd. Gunvor has moved to mothball its processing units and keep the site as a trading terminal, while LyondellBasell/Covestro on Maasvlakte and Tronox in Botlek have announced closures. Tank storage under Vopak, VTTI, Odfjell, HES and Evos, plus the Porthos CO2 line injecting from autumn 2026, add continuing scope.

EN ISO 9712 NDT personnel certification (Hobéon SKO recognised schemes)

name: Antwerp
companies: TotalEnergies Antwerp Refining and Petrochemical Platform
industrialProfile: Antwerp is Europe's largest integrated chemical cluster: seven of the world's ten biggest chemical companies produce here, with more than 200 firms linked by shared pipeline racks and the port handling 27.5 million tonnes of chemical cargo in 2024. BASF Antwerpen alone runs 54 production plants on 600 hectares, the group's second-largest site worldwide. TotalEnergies' platform pairs Europe's third-largest refinery at 338,000 bpd with crackers and a polymer plant, though one of its two crackers is slated to close by end-2027. ExxonMobil's Antwerp refinery runs about 320,000 bpd with a coker. INEOS Project ONE, a €3 billion-plus ethane cracker rated above 1.45 million tonnes of ethylene a year, targets mechanical completion late 2026 and start-up in early 2027.

name: Kuwait
companies: Kuwait Integrated Petroleum Industries Company (KIPIC) — Al-Zour
industrialProfile: Kuwait's inspection demand is concentrated in one state-owned chain. KIPIC's Al-Zour refinery, about 90 km south of Kuwait City, has reached its full 615,000 b/d rate, making it the second largest in the Middle East. KNPC's Clean Fuels Project reconfigured Mina Abdullah to 454,000 b/d and Mina Al-Ahmadi to 346,000 b/d, running the pair as a roughly 800,000 b/d merchant complex, and retired the 200,000 b/d Shuaiba refinery in April 2017. Upstream, Kuwait Oil Company operates Burgan and the northern fields from Ahmadi, while EQUATE and Petrochemical Industries Company run the Shuaiba ethylene, polyethylene and glycol complex.

Imperial Oil's Nanticoke refinery, Ontario's second largest, processed about 103,000 barrels a day in 2025 and supplies roughly a quarter of the petroleum products sold in Ontario. Immediately adjacent, Stelco's Lake Erie Works, the newest integrated steel mill in North America and Cleveland-Cliffs-owned since November 2024, runs a blast furnace, BOF and hot strip mill; Cliffs is fitting a new blast furnace stove and charging hot-briquetted iron, with capital work scheduled through 2027. The 3,964 MW coal-fired Nanticoke Generating Station closed in 2013 and its site now carries the 44 MW Nanticoke Solar Facility, an OPG joint venture with Six Nations of the Grand River and the Mississaugas of the Credit.

Vale Base Metals operates five underground mines — Coleman, Copper Cliff, Creighton, Garson and Totten — feeding the Clarabelle Mill, the Copper Cliff Smelter commissioned in 1930, and the Copper Cliff Nickel Refinery. The Superstack, retired in 2020 after the roughly $1 billion Clean AER project, began a five-year dismantling in September 2025. Glencore's Sudbury Integrated Nickel Operations run Fraser Mine, the Strathcona Mill and the Sudbury Smelter at Falconbridge, which produces nickel matte for Nikkelverk in Norway and is getting a new furnace costing over $100 million. KGHM's Victoria project, 35 km west, would mill through Clarabelle.

Stellantis restored a third shift at Windsor Assembly in February 2026, lifting employment to nearly 6,000 building the Chrysler Pacifica, Voyager and Grand Caravan alongside the Dodge Charger Daytona and SIXPACK. NextStar Energy's battery cell plant, Canada's first at commercial scale, opened in March 2026 with roughly 1,300 hired; Stellantis sold its 49% stake to LG Energy Solution weeks earlier. Ford is spending C$700 million at the Essex Engine Plant to add 6.7L and 7.3L V8 lines beside the existing 5.0L. Beyond autos, the Ojibway rock salt mine can produce up to 3 million tonnes a year and Hiram Walker & Sons is North America's largest beverage distillery.

Thunder Bay Pulp and Paper ended newsprint production in the first quarter of 2026, cutting 150 jobs, and now runs its Neebing Avenue site as a single-line softwood kraft mill that also sells cogenerated power to the Ontario grid. Alstom's plant has built GO Transit's bi-level coaches for nearly fifty years and holds a C$500 million Metrolinx contract to overhaul 181 of them from 2026, plus a Toronto subway car order. The port is the Seaway's largest outbound terminal: eight elevators run by Richardson, Viterra, Cargill and G3 moved 7.26 million tonnes of grain in 2023, and Thunder Bay Terminals handles coal, potash and petroleum coke.

The Portlands Energy Centre, a 550 MW gas-fired station at 470 Unwin Avenue owned by OPG and operated by Atura Power, is the city's only large generator. Ashbridges Bay is Canada's second-largest wastewater plant at 818,000 cubic metres a day. Sanofi's Connaught Campus added an $800 million, 200,000-square-foot vaccine plant with a second facility due in 2027, and Enwave's Deep Lake Water Cooling loop reached 60 MW after its 2024 expansion, cooling about 180 downtown buildings.

Ford's Oakville Assembly Complex, employing about 4,079, was retooled away from a three-row EV and begins building F-Series Super Duty pickups in 2026 — up to 100,000 units a year and roughly 1,800 jobs, with an electrified Super Duty later in the decade. Collins Aerospace employs around 1,500 on aerospace parts. The pressure and welded work sits in smaller shops: Zeton designs and fabricates modular pilot and demonstration plants, IPEX manufactures piping systems, Samuel, Son & Co. processes metals and Mancor Industries makes heavy metal components. Dare Foods, founded here in 1919 and still headquartered on Kingsway Drive, is the largest plant, with Mitchell Plastics in injection moulding and Krug making office and healthcare furniture. Kitchener Utilities is unusual — a municipally owned natural gas distribution system, one of very few left in Ontario, run alongside city water and sewer. The heavy inspection work is minutes away in Cambridge: BWXT Canada is headquartered there, has supplied over 305 CANDU and PWR steam generators, houses one of the world's largest nuclear clean rooms and is adding C$80 million of capacity; Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada employs roughly 8,500 across Cambridge and Woodstock; ATS Corporation builds factory automation.

Algoma Steel fired its first electric arc in July 2025, ending 124 years of blast furnace and coke oven steelmaking; the C$880 million conversion runs two 250-tonne EAFs rated at 3.7 million tons of liquid steel a year and cuts the plant's carbon footprint by up to 70%. On the same Industrial Centre, Tenaris Algoma Tubes makes seamless casing and, since 2022, ERW pipe, and is spending $305.9 million on modernization with $76.2 million of federal funding announced in May 2026. Imperial's Kearl mine, pushed toward 300,000 bbl/d, Suncor's Fort Hills near 180,000 bbl/d and Canadian Natural's Albian Muskeg River and Jackpine mines ship bitumen rather than upgrade it. Coke drums, hydrotreaters, froth-treatment vessels, tailings lines and slurry piping carry the work, concentrated into spring and autumn turnarounds.

CESSCO Fabrication & Engineering, operating since 1948, rolls shell courses up to eight inches thick and builds vessels to 36 feet diameter and 750 tons; Penfabco has run a dedicated pressure-vessel shop here since 1968; Edmonton Exchanger rebuilds heat exchangers and vessel components. PCL's Nisku fabrication facility, about 145,000 square feet, feeds an adjacent 72-acre module yard, and finished modules move north on Alberta's nine-metre high-load corridor. Keyera and Enbridge crude and NGL terminals ring the city's east side.

TC Energy, Enbridge, Pembina, Cenovus and Suncor run pipeline and integrity programmes from here, and EPC firms such as Bantrel scope Alberta turnarounds from Calgary offices. Shell's Scotford complex immediately north-east runs an LC-Fining bitumen upgrader rated near 328,000 bbl/d alongside a refinery and a chemicals plant, with the Quest CCS unit attached to the upgrader. Dow's Fort Saskatchewan site makes ethylene and polyethylene with about 500 staff and 300 contractors, and is building the Path2Zero net-zero expansion. Inter Pipeline's Heartland Petrochemical Complex converts propane into 525,000 tonnes a year of polypropylene, Keyera fractionates and caverns NGLs, and Nutrien's Redwater nitrogen complex lies just north. Sherritt's nickel-cobalt refinery here has been idle since June 2026.

Beside it the Lloydminster refinery processes roughly 27,000 bbl/d of heavy crude and is Canada's largest single asphalt supplier, and a 130-million-litre-a-year wheat ethanol plant shares the site. Surrounding cold-flow and thermal heavy oil production feeds the complex. Beyond it and the associated service and fabrication yards, the city's industrial base is genuinely thin.

Olymel's hog plant, among Canada's largest and most modern, processes over 45,000 hogs a week with more than 1,400 staff, putting ammonia refrigeration and stainless process piping into the local inspection load. Third, Red Deer is central Alberta's oilfield-equipment manufacturing base, where shops such as Red Deer Ironworks fabricate high-pressure flow control and wellsite packages. NOVA's Joffre complex sits fifteen kilometres east.

Dow holds a half interest in the third cracker, E3, a stake that generated nearly two decades of litigation. The adjacent 474-MW Joffre cogeneration plant, owned by TransAlta, Capital Power and NOVA, supplies power and steam. Headcount exceeds 800 permanent staff and 1,200 contractors during turnarounds.

Cancarb, part of the Tokai Carbon group, runs the world's largest thermal carbon black plant at 54,000 tonnes a year across six units and exports waste-heat power to the city grid. Keyera's Alberta EnviroFuels plant, the world's largest iso-octane producer, sits in the same county. Work here is turnaround-driven, and the Strathcona Industrial Association coordinates monitoring across the cluster.

name: Belle Chasse
companies: Harvest Midstream Belle Chasse Terminal (former Phillips 66 Alliance Refinery)
industrialProfile: Belle Chasse changed shape after Hurricane Ida. Phillips 66 chose not to rebuild the Alliance Refinery, converting it to a terminal and selling it to Harvest Midstream in February 2023 — about 3,200 acres with roughly 1 million barrels of active storage and two crude docks. That shifted local inspection work off process units and onto API 653 tankage, transfer piping and marine loading arms. Chevron Oronite's Oak Point plant, on 100 west-bank acres since 1943, still makes fuel and lubricant additives and claims to supply about 16% of the world market. NAS JRB New Orleans sits in town, and Venture Global's 36-train Plaquemines LNG, nameplated at 20 MTPA and approved to 27.2, runs downriver at Port Sulphur.

name: Saraland
industrialProfile: Saraland anchors the southern end of Alabama's MAST chemical corridor — McIntosh, Axis, Saraland, Theodore — at the head of Mobile Bay. Its centrepiece is the former Shell Mobile Chemical complex, bought by Vertex Energy in 2022 for $75 million and now Vertex Refining Alabama, a roughly 75,000–90,000 b/d refining and petrochemical site producing LPG, gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, low-sulphur VGO and benzene. Vertex converted a hydrocracker to renewable diesel, reversed it to conventional service in October 2024, and emerged from Chapter 11 in 2025 owned by its lenders. Alabama Power's coal- and gas-fired Plant Barry sits across the Mobile River at Bucks; Kimberly-Clark's Mobile tissue mill and its on-site CHP plant are minutes away.

name: Axis
industrialProfile: Axis is a chemical-corridor town rather than a metro — a handful of plants on the Mobile River north of Saraland, and essentially nothing else industrial. Arkema operates the 730-acre former Stauffer LeMoyne site here, with a 100-acre working plant, about 128 employees and round-the-clock production across three chemistries: acrylic impact modifiers and process aids, PEKK, and tin-based organometallics. AMVAC leases 25 acres for manufacturing, formulating and packaging inside a 510-acre complex sharing common services with DuPont. Ten miles north at McIntosh, Olin still runs diaphragm-cell chlorine and caustic soda after permanently retiring roughly half that capacity in 2021. Inspection work is reactor, column, exchanger and transfer-line integrity on continuous-run plants.

name: Bay Minette
industrialProfile: Bay Minette's industrial base was furniture and light manufacturing — Standard Furniture with over 1.25 million square feet of warehousing and distribution, plus Quincy Compressor and DentalEZ — until Novelis chose the town for the first fully integrated aluminium recycling and rolling plant built in North America in more than 40 years. The multibillion-dollar Baldwin County site is sized at 600 kt of finished goods, about 420 kt of it beverage can sheet, with the cold mill commissioning and full startup scheduled through the second half of 2026. That one project reorders local demand toward greenfield construction QA — structural steel welds, process and utility piping, furnace and mill-stand fabrication — ahead of steady-state rolling-mill inspection.

name: Panama City
industrialProfile: Panama City's industry is shipbuilding and line pipe. Eastern Shipbuilding Group works yards at Panama City, Allanton and Port St. Joe, including the Nelson yard's 420-foot deep-water pier used for final outfitting, commissioning, dock and sea trials. Alongside it at Port Panama City, Borusan Berg Pipe rolls longitudinally welded large-diameter line pipe from 24 to 64 inches on a 12-metre three-roll bending line, double-jointing to 24 metres and coating on site — API 5L seam inspection at production volume. WestRock's 645,000-ton containerboard and fluff pulp mill closed permanently in June 2022, leaving 350 heavy-industrial acres in redevelopment next to the shipyard. Tyndall AFB and Naval Support Activity Panama City add defence work.

name: Pensacola
industrialProfile: Pensacola's heavy industry sits inland at Cantonment. Ascend Performance Materials' plant on Old Chemstrand Road makes nylon 6,6 and its full precursor chain — acrylonitrile, adiponitrile, adipic acid and hexamethylenediamine — and kept operating normally through a Chapter 11 that ended in December 2025. International Paper's Pensacola mill on Muscogee Road produces fluff pulp and containerboard. On the coast the work is aviation rather than process: ST Engineering's MRO at Pensacola International Airport runs hangars with eight wide-body and ten narrow-body bays, and NAS Pensacola hosts Naval Air Technical Training. The metro therefore carries two distinct inspection populations — PSM-covered fixed equipment inland, Part 145 airframe NDT on the bay.

name: Tampa
companies: Tampa Electric Big Bend Power Station
industrialProfile: Tampa's industrial demand is phosphate chemistry, fuel terminals and ship repair. Mosaic's Riverview complex on Tampa Bay makes sulphuric acid, phosphoric acid, fluorosilicic acid and ammoniated phosphate fertilizers — roughly 800,000 tons of phosphoric acid and 1.6 million tons of processed phosphate a year — with an operating East phosphogypsum stack now under a federal hazardous-waste settlement. Forty to fifty percent of all petroleum products entering Florida land at Port Tampa Bay, feeding a dense tank-terminal cluster. TECO's Big Bend station on some 1,500 acres converted Unit 1 to gas combined cycle in 2023 and retired Unit 2 in 2021. International Ship Repair operates three floating drydocks; Gulf Marine Repair works four on a 50-acre yard.

name: Port Manatee
companies: Air Products LNG heat exchanger plant
industrialProfile: Port Manatee's standout is fabrication, not cargo. Air Products builds coil-wound LNG heat exchangers — small to very large — in roughly 390,000 square feet on the port at Palmetto, shipping ASME Section VIII pressure equipment out to liquefaction trains worldwide; radiography, ultrasonics and PT on those welds are the highest-value inspection work anywhere on Tampa Bay's south shore. Around it, Kinder Morgan and TransMontaigne run liquid tank terminals, Mosaic moves phosphate over its own berth, and Logistec, SAC Cement, Ames Salt and Fresh Del Monte handle dry, bulk and refrigerated cargo. Piney Point, the closed phosphogypsum stack immediately adjacent, keeps engineered-containment monitoring on the local agenda.

name: Jacksonville
industrialProfile: Jacksonville is a ship-repair town with a steel mill attached. BAE Systems opened a $250 million shiplift and land-level repair complex in June 2025 that lifts vessels displacing up to 25,000 tons and holds several ashore simultaneously, roughly tripling yard capability for Mayport-homeported Navy ships and commercial callers into the Port of Jacksonville. General Dynamics NASSCO-Mayport serves the same fleet as a Master Ship Repair facility. CMC Steel Florida — bought from Gerdau in 2018 — runs an EAF long-products mill of about 617,000 tonnes crude capacity making coiled rebar and wire rod, and is JEA's largest single-site customer. JEA's Northside Generating Station is rated near 1,300 MW; Anheuser-Busch's 1.4-million-square-foot brewery adds process work.

name: Brunswick
companies: Georgia Ports Authority Colonel's Island Terminal
industrialProfile: Brunswick's base is narrow and got narrower. Georgia-Pacific's Brunswick Cellulose mill, around 600 employees, is the one large process plant — fluff pulp with over 83% exported, and an annual outage that concentrates most of the year's fixed-equipment inspection into a few weeks. Pinova's resin and rosin plant, 213 jobs, never reopened after an April 2023 fire, removing the town's other chemical site. What is growing is logistics and aviation: Georgia Ports' Colonel's Island terminal spans over 1,700 acres with 3,355 feet of continuous berthing and 637 acres of paved storage, passing Baltimore as the busiest US roll-on/roll-off auto and machinery port in 2024, and Gulfstream's Brunswick service centre and completions hangars hold up to 16 large-cabin jets.

name: Savannah
companies: Port of Savannah Garden City Terminal
industrialProfile: Savannah's industrial mix is shifting out of pulp and into aerospace and automotive. Gulfstream Aerospace — the Southeast's largest aerospace manufacturer, about 13,000 employees — builds, completes and services large-cabin business jets here, driving penetrant, magnetic-particle and ultrasonic work under NAS 410 and Nadcap. Hyundai Motor Group's $7.6 billion Metaplant America, 25 miles west on I-16, spans more than 16 million square feet and is sized for up to 500,000 EVs and hybrids a year. Georgia-Pacific's Savannah River Mill runs at Rincon and Georgia Power's Plant McIntosh in Effingham County generates 1.38 GW with a proposed expansion toward 3 GW. International Paper announced in 2025 it is closing its Savannah and Riceboro mills.

name: Charleston
companies: Dominion Energy South Carolina LNG facility
Naval Nuclear Power Training Command (Goose Creek)
industrialProfile: Charleston harbour's industry is terminals and marine logistics rather than heavy process plant — worth saying plainly, because the state's refineries and mills sit elsewhere. SC Ports runs four public terminals at a 45-foot draft across Charleston, North Charleston and Mount Pleasant, with privately owned facilities handling petroleum, coal and steel. Odfjell operates a bulk-liquid chemical storage terminal on the Cooper River; Kinder Morgan works a 60-acre dry-bulk terminal rated near 2.5 million tons a year alongside a 148-acre liquids tank terminal. Dominion Energy's LNG plant near Charleston stores about 1.0 Bcf equivalent and can regasify roughly 6% of storage per day. Naval Nuclear Power Training Command and its moored training ships operate at Goose Creek.

name: North Charleston
industrialProfile: North Charleston carries the Lowcountry's manufacturing weight. Boeing South Carolina is the sole global final-assembly site for the 787 Dreamliner and broke ground in November 2025 on a $1 billion campus expansion to lift build rates. Detyens Shipyards, on the former Charleston Naval Shipyard, is among the largest commercial repair yards on the US East Coast, with 33 marine and industrial firms sharing the site. Mercedes-Benz Vans in Ladson has assembled over 430,000 Sprinter, Metris and eSprinter vans since 2006. Ingevity's plant, operating since the 1940s, is investing $53.3 million.
