In adjacent Berkeley County, Nucor Steel Berkeley rolls up to 3.5 million tons of sheet and structural steel and Century Aluminum's Mt. Holly smelter is nameplated near 230,000 tonnes.
localCompliance: NAVSEA Standard Items / ABS class rules

name: North Salt Lake
companies: Big West Oil North Salt Lake Refinery (FJ Management)
Chevron Salt Lake Refinery (adjacent, across the county line)
HF Sinclair Woods Cross Refinery (three miles north)
Rio Tinto Kennecott Garfield smelter (Magna, west across the valley)
industrialProfile: North Salt Lake is a Davis County city of about 22,000 sitting at the south end of the Wasatch Front refining corridor. Big West Oil, a wholly owned FJ Management subsidiary, runs the city's anchor plant: a medium-to-high conversion refinery rated near 35,000 b/cd, staffed by roughly 250 people, processing Utah, Wyoming, Colorado and Canadian crude into motor fuels and specialty products for seven western states. Chevron's Salt Lake refinery sits immediately south across the county line and HF Sinclair's Woods Cross plant three miles north, so tank farms, products terminals and pipeline manifolds along I-15 dominate the local industrial footprint far more than discrete manufacturing does.

name: Woods Cross
companies: Silver Eagle Refining, Woods Cross (The International Group)
HF Sinclair Woods Cross products terminal
industrialProfile: Woods Cross is a Davis County city of about 11,000 whose industrial identity is essentially one refinery complex. HF Sinclair's Woods Cross refinery, physically straddling the West Bountiful line, runs 45,000 b/cd of regional sweet and Uinta Basin waxy crude plus pipelined Canadian barrels, and typically blends another 2,000 b/d of natural gasoline, butane and gas oil on top of nameplate. It is a high-conversion plant, and its products move north to terminals at Boise, Burley and Spokane and south on the 399-mile UNEV pipeline to the Las Vegas Valley. Silver Eagle Refining's small waxy-crude plant, now under The International Group, operates in the same town.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section VIII and Section V

name: Sinclair
companies: HF Sinclair Sinclair renewable diesel unit
Power Company of Wyoming Chokecherry and Sierra Madre Wind Energy Project
Union Pacific Overland Route main line
industrialProfile: Sinclair is a company town of roughly 400 people built around the refinery that renamed it from Parco. HF Sinclair's Sinclair refinery runs 94,000 b/cd of Canadian and domestic sweet and sour crude, making it one of the largest in the Rockies, and carries a co-located 10,000 b/d renewable diesel unit with approved LCFS pathways in California and British Columbia. The plant employs more than 500 people, and Union Pacific's Overland Route main line and Interstate 80 run past the tank farm. Immediately south, Anschutz's Power Company of Wyoming is building the Chokecherry and Sierra Madre wind project toward 3,000 MW of nameplate capacity across 320,000 acres in Carbon County.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section VIII and Section V

name: Newcastle
companies: Wyoming Refining Company Newcastle Refinery (Par Pacific)
Par Pacific Newcastle products pipeline to Rapid City
industrialProfile: Newcastle is a Weston County town of about 3,400 on the western edge of the Black Hills, and its industrial base is genuinely narrow: one refinery, bentonite, and Powder River Basin oilfield service. Par Pacific's Wyoming Refining Company plant has stood on Main Street since 1927, occupies roughly 121 fee-owned acres and runs 18,000 to 20,000 b/cd at a Nelson complexity near 10.7, using crude distillation, a catalytic cracker, naphtha hydrotreating and reforming to make gasoline, ULSD and jet fuel that moves toward Rapid City. Fifteen miles northwest around Upton, Osage and Clay Spur, Black Hills Bentonite and other operators mine and mill Wyoming sodium bentonite.

name: Artesia
companies: HF Sinclair Navajo Refining Company, Artesia
HF Sinclair Artesia renewable diesel and pretreatment units
Targa Resources Artesia gathering and processing system
Targa Resources South Carlsbad gas processing system
industrialProfile: Artesia is the refining centre of the New Mexico Permian. HF Sinclair's Navajo refinery on East Main runs roughly 100,000 b/cd of sweet and sour Permian crude, operates in tandem with a companion crude unit at Lovington about 40 miles east, and supplies New Mexico, Arizona and West Texas. A feedstock pretreatment unit and a 9,000 b/d renewable diesel unit were completed on the Artesia site in 2022. HF Sinclair Navajo employs around 575 people across Eddy, Lea and Bernalillo counties. Surrounding Eddy County carries Targa's Artesia and South Carlsbad gathering and cryogenic processing systems, part of roughly 1.4 Bcf/d of northern Delaware Basin capacity, plus dense crude and produced-water gathering.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section VIII Division 1 and Section V

name: Gallup
companies: Marathon Petroleum Gallup terminal (former Ciniza/Gallup refinery)
BNSF Railway Southern Transcon main line
Gallup Energy Logistics Park (Gallup Land Partners)
industrialProfile: Gallup's industrial base narrowed sharply in 2020 and it is honest to say so. The Ciniza refinery east of town, built by El Paso Natural Gas and later run by Shell, Giant, Western and finally Marathon, processed about 26,000 b/cd until Marathon idled it in April 2020 and made the closure permanent that August, cutting roughly 200 jobs. The site now functions as a products terminal rather than a refinery, so tankage and loading rack work is what remains. What still moves is freight: Gallup sits on BNSF's Southern Transcon, and the 2,500-acre Gallup Energy Logistics Park five miles northwest holds a BNSF-certified 365-acre site with about 20,000 linear feet of track and coal transloading loops.

name: Tucson
industrialProfile: Tucson's industrial base is missiles and copper. RTX's Missiles & Defense business is headquartered on the south side beside Tucson International and is Arizona's third-largest industrial employer, with something on the order of 10,000 to 13,000 people building missile hardware. Davis-Monthan AFB hosts the 309th AMARG boneyard, while Bombardier's Tucson Service Centre on Aero Park Boulevard and Ascent Aviation at Tucson International and Pinal Airpark run heavy airframe maintenance. South of the city, ASARCO's Mission mine at Sahuarita and Freeport-McMoRan's Sierrita mine at Green Valley are large open-pit copper operations. Caterpillar moved its Surface Mining & Technology headquarters to a Tucson campus in 2019; TEP's Sundt station now runs entirely on gas.

name: Yuma
companies: General Motors Desert Proving Ground Yuma
industrialProfile: Yuma's inspection demand comes from test ranges and agriculture rather than heavy process plants, and the metro has no refinery, mill or shipyard. Yuma Proving Ground, an Army Test and Evaluation Command site headquartered about 30 miles north across western Yuma and southwestern La Paz counties, is the county's largest single civilian employer and hosts General Motors' Desert Proving Ground on leased land inside the range. MCAS Yuma is the busiest air station in the Marine Corps and supports roughly 80 percent of the Corps' air-to-ground aviation training. Gowan Company, a family-owned agrochemical group, is headquartered downtown and formulates through Gowan Milling. Union Pacific's Sunset Route and the rail-served Asher Inland Port carry the freight.

name: El Paso
companies: Union Pacific Santa Teresa intermodal and fueling facility
El Paso Electric Newman Generating Station
El Paso Electric Rio Grande Power Station, Sunland Park
industrialProfile: El Paso runs one refinery, one very large Army post and a cross-border manufacturing corridor. Marathon's El Paso refinery processes about 131,000 b/cd of Permian crude through catalytic cracking, alkylation and reforming, supplying West Texas, southern New Mexico and Arizona; a single recent turnaround there ran roughly $130 million. Fort Bliss is the metro's largest employer, with more than 40,000 military and civilian personnel. Union Pacific's Santa Teresa complex, eight miles west across the New Mexico line, combines an intermodal ramp, fueling station, crew-change facilities and a switching yard serving Juarez maquiladora traffic. El Paso Electric operates the gas-fired Newman station north of the city and the Rio Grande station at Sunland Park.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section VIII and Section V

name: Kern County
companies: California Resources Corporation Elk Hills Field and Elk Hills Power Plant
Kern Energy (formerly Kern Oil & Refining) Bakersfield refinery
Global Clean Energy Bakersfield Renewable Fuels
industrialProfile: Kern County spans roughly 8,000 square miles and holds about three-quarters of California's producing oil wells, so demand is spread across an oil province rather than a single city. Chevron works most of the Kern River heavy-oil field on cyclic steam; California Resources operates Elk Hills with the adjacent 550 MW Elk Hills combined-cycle cogeneration plant, the target of its CalCapture CO2 project. Two refineries remain: Kern Energy at Bakersfield, the only refiner between San Francisco and Los Angeles making gasoline and diesel, and Global Clean Energy's Bakersfield Renewable Fuels plant, converted from the former Alon refinery and running about 250,000 gallons a day of renewable diesel since 2024. Aerospace sits east at Mojave Air and Space Port.
localCompliance: Cal/OSHA PSM for Petroleum Refineries, Title 8 Section 5189.1
ASME BPVC Section VIII and Section V

name: Santa Maria
companies: Vandenberg Space Force Base (SLC-4E, SpaceX Falcon 9)
The Okonite Company Santa Maria cable plant
Phillips 66 Santa Maria Refinery (closed 2023, in demolition and remediation)
industrialProfile: Santa Maria's heavy industry has thinned and the honest picture is a narrow one. Phillips 66 shut the 1,780-acre Santa Maria refinery on the Nipomo Mesa in January 2023 after 65 years, and San Luis Obispo County approved demolition and remediation in October 2024, so refinery-side work here is decommissioning: tank and piping teardown plus cleanup of about 200 acres of contaminated soil and groundwater. What still runs is Vandenberg Space Force Base 25 miles west, the West Coast's polar-orbit spaceport with SpaceX Falcon 9 operations from SLC-4E; The Okonite Company's wire and cable plant, over 545,000 square feet on a 50-acre site; and Melfred Borzall, which builds horizontal directional drilling tooling locally.

name: Paramount
companies: World Energy Paramount (former AltAir Paramount / Paramount Petroleum)
industrialProfile: Paramount packs an unusual amount of heavy industry into 4.7 square miles of Los Angeles County: renewable fuels plus aerospace forging. World Energy holds the former Paramount Petroleum and AltAir site, a 66-acre complex that once refined 39,500 b/d of crude and now makes renewable diesel, renewable gasoline and sustainable aviation fuel from waste oils, fats and greases for United Airlines, UPS, Boeing and the Defense Department. Four forge shops operate in the same city: Weber Metals, an Otto Fuchs company running a $180 million, 60,000-ton (540 MN) pull-down die press whose first production part was a 737 MAX main landing gear beam; Carlton Forge Works, a Precision Castparts seamless rolled ring producer; plus Press Forge and Mattco Forge.
localCompliance: AMS-STD-2154 ultrasonic inspection of wrought metals

name: Wilmington
companies: Amtrak Wilmington Shops and Bear Maintenance Facility
Calpine Edge Moor and Hay Road Energy Center
industrialProfile: Wilmington is a chemicals and rail town rather than a heavy-manufacturing one, and it is distinct from Delaware City 12 miles south, which holds the PBF refinery. Chemours is headquartered here, and the DuPont Experimental Station on the Brandywine remains the principal R&D site for both DuPont and Chemours, now with multiple industrial tenants. Croda's Atlas Point plant at New Castle, built on the Delaware River in 1937 as a gunpowder works, runs surfactant and ethylene oxide production with roughly 240 USW-represented employees. Amtrak's Wilmington Shops overhaul all Northeast Corridor electric locomotives and Amfleet cars. Calpine's Edge Moor and Hay Road complex generates at least 698 MW on gas into PJM, and Port Wilmington works 308 acres of deep-water terminal.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section VIII Division 1 and Section V

name: Delaware City
companies: Air Products hydrogen SMR at Delaware City
Formosa Plastics Corporation Delaware (Delaware City PVC plant)
industrialProfile: Delaware City is a town of about 1,900 that hosts one of the largest refineries on the East Coast, and it should not be confused with Wilmington 12 miles north. PBF Energy's Delaware City refinery runs roughly 180,000 to 190,000 b/cd at a Nelson complexity near 13.6, with a fluid coking unit, an FCC, a hydrocracker with hydrogen plant, a continuous catalytic reformer, two alkylation units and multiple hydrotreaters, a configuration built for heavy sour crude. Air Products bought the site's steam methane reformer from PBF in 2020 and supplies hydrogen under long-term contract. A rail crude terminal completed in 2013 brings barrels in by unit train, and Formosa Plastics runs a 400-acre PVC plant on School House Road.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section VIII Division 1 and Section V

name: El Dorado
companies: Frontier El Dorado Refining cogeneration turbine
industrialProfile: El Dorado is a one-refinery town in Butler County, thirty miles east of Wichita. HF Sinclair's El Dorado refinery runs 135,000 bpd — the largest in Kansas and the only survivor of the eight refineries the county once held — taking Cushing-sourced and Canadian crude by pipeline and shipping product toward Denver and mid-continent markets. It carries its own 39 MW gas turbine on site. Around the fence line sit BG Products' automotive chemical plant, Barton Solvents' El Dorado solvent terminal and packaging works, and oilfield service firms left over from the 1915 El Dorado field. Work here is turnaround-shaped: crude, FCC and hydrotreater equipment, tankage and rack piping.

name: McPherson
industrialProfile: McPherson carries an unusually deep industrial base for a city of 14,000. The CHS refinery — the farmer-owned National Cooperative Refinery Association plant since 1943 — was lifted toward 100,000 bpd by a $327 million expansion and feeds CHS pipelines and terminals across the Plains. Pfizer's McPherson site, acquired with Hospira in 2015, fills sterile injectables and filled Comirnaty doses, running clean-room utilities, autoclaves and lyophilizers. Johns Manville and CertainTeed operate fiberglass insulation lines with high-temperature melters, while Westlake Pipe & Fittings and Viega add pipe and fitting production. Inspection demand splits cleanly between refinery turnarounds and regulated pharmaceutical utility systems.

name: Coffeyville
industrialProfile: Coffeyville sits on the Kansas–Oklahoma line and runs on one integrated CVR Energy complex. The refinery processes roughly 115,000 bpd of medium and heavy sour crude, and its petroleum coke feeds the adjacent Coffeyville nitrogen fertilizer plant — the only North American nitrogen producer gasifying petcoke, with an 89 MMscfd hydrogen capacity gasifier train, a 1,300 ton-per-day ammonia unit and a 3,100 ton-per-day UAN unit. Outside the fence, John Deere Coffeyville Works machines drivetrain components, Acme Foundry pours gray-iron castings for diesel engines and hydraulic valves across 300,000 square feet with 300-plus employees, and Star Pipe Products and Bartlett Milling fill out the industrial park.

name: Ponca City
industrialProfile: Ponca City is built around the refinery E.W. Marland founded in 1914, now Phillips 66's Ponca City plant at about 200,000 bpd — crude distilling, naphtha reforming, fluid catalytic cracking, alkylation, hydrodesulfurization and delayed coking, producing a high share of transportation fuels plus anode-grade petroleum coke. Jupiter Sulphur handles the refinery's sulfur on site, and Continental Carbon runs one of its three US carbon black plants here on refinery heavy oil. Beyond hydrocarbons the base is lighter: Dorada Foods cooks chicken products, Air Systems Components builds HVAC components, and Albertsons runs a regional distribution center. Refinery turnaround and tank work dominates.

name: Ardmore
industrialProfile: Ardmore's industrial base narrowed sharply this decade. Valero's Ardmore refinery still runs 87,000 bpd with about 290 employees, taking Permian and Cushing crude on third-party pipelines and making gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, LPG, propylene, sulfur and butane — it remains the metro's only process plant of scale. Michelin North America ended tire production at Ardmore in 2025 after more than fifty years, taking roughly 1,200 jobs with it, though rubber-mixing continues on the site to feed other Michelin plants. What is left is distribution: Dot Foods' cold-storage warehouse, a Dollar General distribution center employing over a thousand, and the Noble Research Institute.

name: Wynnewood
companies: CVR Energy Wynnewood renewable diesel unit
Wynnewood crude gathering and Cushing-area pipeline connections
industrialProfile: Wynnewood is a refinery village in Garvin County, and that is essentially the whole industrial base — worth stating plainly rather than dressing up. CVR Energy's Wynnewood Refining Company plant carries a nameplate capacity of 74,500 bpd and makes gasoline, diesel, military jet fuel, solvents and asphalt. Its renewable diesel unit ran until December 2025, when CVR reverted it to hydrocarbon processing on renewables economics; that conversion and reconversion put an unusual volume of weld, piping and vessel work through a town of a couple of thousand people. There is no second plant, mill or utility station here — surrounding work is gathering lines, tank batteries and lease equipment.

name: Borger
industrialProfile: Borger is a Panhandle hydrocarbon town built on three large plants roughly 50 miles northeast of Amarillo. Phillips 66's Borger refinery runs 149,000 bpd of mainly medium sour crude and NGL piped from West Texas, the Panhandle and Canada, with crude distilling, naphtha reforming, FCC, alkylation, hydrodesulfurization and delayed coking, plus about 22,500 bpd of NGL fractionation; Phillips 66 moved to full ownership of the former WRB joint-venture interest. Chevron Phillips Chemical's Borger plant, commercial since 1956, makes more than sixty compounds — organosulfur chemicals, high-purity hydrocarbons, solvents, performance fuels and mining chemicals. Nutrien's Borger Nitrogen Operations added a $720 million, 610,000-tonne urea plant in 2017.

name: McKee (Sunray)
companies: Moore County Panhandle gas gathering and NGL lines
industrialProfile: McKee is a refinery rather than a town: Valero's Panhandle plant on FM 119 outside Sunray in Moore County, 45 miles north of Amarillo. Built in 1933 and now processing 200,000 bpd with about 376 employees, it makes gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, asphalt, carbon black oil, sulfur, sulfuric acid and LPG. Continental Carbon runs a Sunray carbon black plant nearby on heavy refinery oil. At Cactus, JBS operates a beef plant employing more than 3,600, now in a $150 million fabrication-floor and ground-beef expansion carrying large ammonia refrigeration systems. The 2007 propane release and fire at McKee still shapes how mechanical integrity scope is written here.

name: Wichita Falls
industrialProfile: Wichita Falls builds aerospace metal and process equipment rather than running process plant, which makes its inspection profile unlike the refinery towns south and west of it. Howmet Aerospace's Wichita Falls Operations produces investment castings and aerospace components for jet engines. Vitro Architectural Glass — the former PPG flat-glass plant, about 322 people at the handover — added a jumbo magnetron-sputtered coater billed as the largest of its kind in North America. Tranter engineers and builds plate heat exchangers from its Wichita Falls headquarters, and Westlake Pipe & Fittings is adding a 190,000 square foot PVCO pipe plant on Industrial Drive. Sheppard AFB hosts the 82nd Training Wing and ENJJPT.

name: Great Bend
industrialProfile: Great Bend's industrial base is genuinely narrow and better named than inflated: oilfield service, one contract chemical manufacturer and light fabrication. Barton County was Kansas's fourth-largest oil producer in 2024 at 1,408,177 barrels, 5.2 percent of state output, but these are stripper wells producing under fifteen barrels a day and often under five, with only 23 new wells drilled in 2025 — so the work is tank batteries, flowlines, pumping units and workover rigs, not process plant. Fuller Industries contract-manufactures cleaning chemicals and aerosols in town; Superior Essex Communications runs a 250-plus employee communications cable plant at Hoisington; Doonan fabricates heavy-haul trailers. No refinery, mill or utility station.

name: Salina
industrialProfile: Salina is a fabrication and food-processing city with no refinery, mill or utility station — its inspection work is weld quality, ammonia refrigeration and structural steel. Schwan's runs the world's largest frozen pizza plant at the Salina Regional Airport Industrial Center, making Tony's, Red Baron and Freschetta from a site grown from 18,000 square feet to nearly a million, with about 1,600 employees. Great Plains Manufacturing, Kubota-owned since 2016, builds tillage, seeding and construction equipment across roughly 950 jobs and a 750,000 square foot assembly building bought in 2020. ElDorado builds cutaway buses for Forest River; Vortex Global makes bulk-solids slide gates; Bergkamp builds asphalt maintenance equipment; Geoprobe builds direct-push rigs.

name: Omaha
companies: Omaha Public Power District (North Omaha Station, Nebraska City Station)
MidAmerican Energy Walter Scott Jr. Energy Center
industrialProfile: Omaha's inspection demand is rail, power and food plant rather than refining. Union Pacific is headquartered downtown and the Council Bluffs yards anchor one of the busiest rail corridors in the country; the original Omaha Shops closed in 1988, so the work is rolling stock, bridges and track structure rather than locomotive overhaul. OPPD operates North Omaha Station — Units 1 to 3 on gas, Units 4 and 5 still on coal with conversion pushed toward 2028 — plus Nebraska City Station, while MidAmerican's Walter Scott Jr. Energy Center across the river holds 1,480 MW on Units 3 and 4. Fort Calhoun's decade-long, billion-dollar decommissioning to greenfield is finishing.

name: Sioux City
companies: MidAmerican Energy George Neal North & South
industrialProfile: Sioux City's heavy equipment sits twelve miles south along the Missouri at Port Neal. CF Industries' Port Neal complex — an ammonia plant, two urea plants, two nitric acid plants and a UAN plant, rebuilt in a $2 billion expansion completed in 2016 — is the metro's largest pressure-equipment population, with MidAmerican's George Neal North and South energy centers alongside. Protein processing carries the headcount: Seaboard Triumph Foods runs about 20,000 hogs a day at Bridgeport West with roughly 2,000 workers, and Tyson Fresh Meats' Dakota City beef plant across the Nebraska line employs about 4,300. Sabre Industries fabricates transmission and communications structures from a 192,000 square foot plant.

name: Davenport
companies: Rock Island Arsenal Joint Manufacturing & Technology Center
Constellation Quad Cities Clean Energy Center (Cordova, IL)
industrialProfile: Davenport anchors the Quad Cities, where aerospace metal, off-highway equipment, an Army arsenal and a nuclear station all sit within twenty miles of each other. Arconic's Davenport Works at Riverdale is the hub of the company's aerospace plate and sheet business and is building a new casting complex, the 'Pit 10' project, to expand ingot and recycled-aluminum capacity. John Deere Davenport Works builds construction and forestry machines. Rock Island Arsenal, on the island between Davenport and Rock Island, is the largest government-owned weapons manufacturing arsenal in the United States and the region's biggest employer at roughly 6,250. Constellation's Quad Cities station near Cordova runs two GE boiling-water reactors, about 1,880 MW gross.

name: Peoria
companies: Caterpillar (East Peoria, Mossville, Mapleton foundry, Morton)
Liberty Steel & Wire (former Keystone Steel & Wire), Bartonville
industrialProfile: Peoria is a heavy-equipment town. Caterpillar keeps around 12,000 people in the region even after moving its global headquarters to Texas: large dozers at East Peoria, engines at Mossville, parts distribution at Morton, and the Mapleton foundry casting diesel cylinder blocks and other large iron parts. Komatsu ships large off-highway mining trucks from its Peoria mining division. At Bartonville, Liberty Steel & Wire — the former Keystone Steel & Wire — runs one of the world's larger rod and wire mills at close to 800,000 tons a year with about 650 employees. Downriver at Pekin, Alto Ingredients operates two distilleries, a yeast plant and the ICP mill, 250 million gallons a year combined.

name: Marcus Hook
companies: Energy Transfer Marcus Hook Industrial Complex
Braskem America Marcus Hook polypropylene plant
Mariner East 1 / 2 / 2X NGL pipeline system (Energy Transfer)
industrialProfile: Marcus Hook is a one-asset borough on the Delaware River. The Sunoco refinery shut in December 2011 and was rebuilt by Energy Transfer as the Marcus Hook Industrial Complex, eastern terminus of the Mariner East pipelines carrying Marcellus and Utica NGLs. Ethane, propane and butane are fractionated, chilled and stored in five granite caverns mined between 1957 and 1976 holding roughly 2 million barrels, plus six refrigerated tanks adding about 3 million barrels; LPG exports run near 260,000 b/d with expansion toward 420,000 b/d by mid-2027. Braskem America runs polypropylene lines across the road, one line hibernated since 2023, and owns the site's propylene cavern.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section V and Section VIII

name: Trainer
companies: Monroe Energy Trainer Refinery (Delta Air Lines subsidiary)
Energy Transfer Marcus Hook Industrial Complex (adjacent, downriver)
Braskem America Marcus Hook polypropylene plant
industrialProfile: Trainer is a small Delaware County borough built around a single plant: the Trainer refinery, bought from Phillips 66 in April 2012 for $180 million by Monroe Energy, a wholly owned Delta Air Lines subsidiary. It processes roughly 185,000 b/d of crude and is configured to maximise jet fuel, yielding about 52,000 b/d for Delta's East Coast operation. It remains the only US refinery owned by an airline, so unit availability and turnaround scope land directly on an airline's fuel cost line. Crude arrives by ship, barge and rail on the Delaware; Energy Transfer's Marcus Hook NGL complex adjoins the borough immediately downriver.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section V and Section VIII

name: Paulsboro
companies: Paulsboro Marine Terminal (South Jersey Port Corporation)
EEW American Offshore Structures (monopile plant, Chapter 11 since April 2026)
PBF Energy Delaware City Refinery (paired across the river)
industrialProfile: Paulsboro's industrial base is PBF Energy's Paulsboro refinery, a 155,000 b/d Delaware River plant. After PBF idled the smaller crude unit, the FCC, the alkylation unit and a coker in 2020, Paulsboro runs as the lubricant base oil and asphalt half of an integrated East Coast pair with the 180,000 b/d Delaware City refinery, supplying intermediates across the river. Beside it, the Paulsboro Marine Terminal was developed as the first US offshore-wind monopile plant; operator EEW American Offshore Structures filed Chapter 11 in April 2026 after Orsted cancelled Ocean Wind 1 and Shell exited Atlantic Shores, leaving heavy-plate rolling and welding capacity idle on a deepwater berth.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section V and Section VIII

name: Westville
companies: Sunoco / Energy Transfer Eagle Point Terminal, Crown Point Road
Eagle Point Power Generation (Rockland Capital), West Deptford
PBF Energy Paulsboro Refinery (approximately three miles south)
industrialProfile: Westville is a small Gloucester County borough whose heavy industry comes down to one riverfront site, and the honest description is narrow. Sunoco permanently shut the 1,000-acre Eagle Point refinery in February 2010 and demolished the process units. What remains at 1000 Crown Point Road is the Eagle Point products terminal, a Sunoco/Energy Transfer wholesale rack with roughly five million barrels of tankage after a two-million-barrel expansion, and next door the 252 MW Eagle Point Power Generation gas plant, now Rockland Capital-owned, commissioned in 1990 as a 220 MW cogeneration unit selling 900 and 250 psig steam to the refinery. Inspection demand here is tanks, docks, piping and boilers, not process units.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section I and Section VIII

name: Linden
industrialProfile: Linden's industry is one 1,235-acre complex on the Arthur Kill: Phillips 66's Bayway refinery, built in 1909, the northernmost and largest operating refinery on the US East Coast at 275,000 b/d, with a Nelson complexity of 8.1, clean product yield around 92 percent, roughly 695 employees, and a 145,000 b/d fluid catalytic cracker that is the largest in the country. An adjoining plastics plant makes up to 775 million pounds of polypropylene a year, Infineum USA blends lubricant additives on the same site, and the 972 MW Linden Cogeneration plant sells steam and power across the fence. GM's Linden Assembly closed in 2005; what is left is refining, chemicals and power.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section V and Section VIII

name: Bayway
industrialProfile: Bayway is not a municipality. It is the Phillips 66 Bayway refinery inside the city of Linden, New Jersey, on the Arthur Kill about 13 miles southwest of Manhattan, and it is treated here as the plant rather than the city. The site spans roughly 1,235 acres, runs 275,000 b/d of predominantly light sweet crude, and holds the largest fluid catalytic cracker in the United States at 145,000 b/d, alongside crude distilling, naphtha reforming, solvent de-asphalting, hydrodesulfurisation and alkylation units and a polypropylene plant rated to 775 million pounds a year. Around 695 employees plus a large resident contractor base work the complex; turnarounds pull hundreds of extra NDT technicians into Union County.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section V and Section VIII

name: Perth Amboy
companies: Phillips 66 Bayway Refinery (across the Arthur Kill in Linden)
industrialProfile: Perth Amboy's heavy industry is now liquid storage and marine handling rather than manufacturing, and the shift is worth stating plainly. Buckeye Partners bought Chevron's 250-acre asphalt refinery site on the Arthur Kill in 2012 for $260 million and operates it as a gasoline and butane blending and rail-offloading hub with more than four million barrels of tankage and four docks. Kinder Morgan's Perth Amboy terminal adds 80 acres, 113 tanks ranging from 1,190 to 300,000 barrels and about 3.49 million barrels of capacity for fuels, chemicals, biofuels and dry bulk. The steel is gone: Gerdau closed the Perth Amboy melt shop in 2006 and the wire rod rolling mill in 2009.

name: Bridgeport
companies: FuelCell Energy Bridgeport Fuel Cell Park
industrialProfile: Bridgeport's industrial spine is energy, not aerospace. Bridgeport Harbor Station Unit 5, a 485 MW combined-cycle plant built around a GE 7HA.02 gas turbine and heat recovery steam generator, came online in June 2019 and displaced the coal-fired Unit 3, retired in 2021 and since demolished. Beside it, the former Wheelabrator plant, now WIN Waste Innovations Bridgeport and commissioned in 1988, burns roughly 737,000 tons of post-recycled waste a year for about 67 MW. FuelCell Energy's 14.9 MW South End fuel-cell park is being rebuilt with new modules for commercial operation in December 2026. Sikorsky closed its Bridgeport helicopter plant in 2015; what survives of aerospace is subcontract work, led by Rotair Aerospace's rotor-component shop.

name: Groton
companies: General Dynamics Electric Boat, Groton shipyard
General Dynamics Electric Boat Quonset Point, Rhode Island (module fabrication)
industrialProfile: Groton is a submarine town. General Dynamics Electric Boat's Groton yard, headquarters of a company employing more than 27,000, builds Virginia-class attack submarines and Columbia-class ballistic-missile boats, with hull modules barged up the Thames from Quonset Point. In July 2026 Electric Boat took the largest award in its 127-year history, a $76.6 billion package covering nine more Virginia-class and five more Columbia-class boats plus roughly $5 billion for Groton shipyard renovation, against a hiring target of 8,000. Naval Submarine Base New London sits on the Groton bank, driving fleet maintenance work. Pfizer's 175-acre Groton campus, 2.17 million square feet and over 4,000 staff, adds process piping and vessel inspection of a different kind.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section III and Section V

name: Bath
companies: BIW East Brunswick Manufacturing Facility, Brunswick
industrialProfile: Bath Iron Works is effectively the whole industrial base: a dense 60-acre General Dynamics yard on the Kennebec River, one of Maine's largest private employers, and lead yard for the Arleigh Burke DDG-51 program. Flight III hulls in build include Louis H. Wilson Jr. (DDG 126), William Charette (DDG 130), Quentin Walsh (DDG 132), John E. Kilmer (DDG 134) and Richard G. Lugar (DDG 136). Keel-to-weather-deck sections are joined in the 77,000-square-foot Ultrahall, parts and non-structural assemblies come from the East Brunswick Manufacturing Facility at Cook's Corner, and hulls move on the land level transfer facility to waterborne completion at Pier 2, backed by a new $40 million Pier Support Center.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section V and Section VIII

name: Portsmouth
companies: Blackline Midstream Newington refrigerated propane terminal
industrialProfile: Portsmouth's heaviest work is technically across the Piscataqua in Kittery, Maine: Portsmouth Naval Shipyard, established 1800 and the Navy's dedicated yard for overhaul and modernization of Los Angeles- and Virginia-class nuclear attack submarines, employing over 6,500. On the New Hampshire bank at Newington sit Granite Shore Power's 400 MW dual-fuel Newington Station, the retired Schiller Station's 80-acre deep-channel site, the 525 MW Newington Energy combined-cycle plant in service since 2002, and New England's only large-scale refrigerated propane storage terminal with waterborne and rail inbound. Lonza's 813,000-square-foot Pease biologics campus runs 20,000-litre mammalian bioreactors, mid-scale 5,000-litre trains and cell-therapy suites.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section I, V and VIII

name: Newport News
companies: Dominion Terminal Associates coal pier (Alpha Metallurgical Resources / Arch Resources)
industrialProfile: Newport News is a single-employer shipbuilding city. HII's Newport News Shipbuilding, Virginia's largest industrial employer with more than 26,000 shipbuilders, is the only US yard that builds nuclear-powered aircraft carriers: Ford-class CVN-79 John F. Kennedy began sea trials in early 2026 while CVN-80 Enterprise is under construction. The yard also builds Virginia-class submarine modules in teaming with Electric Boat and performs Nimitz-class refueling and complex overhauls. Around it, Liebherr has manufactured ultra-class mining haul trucks in Newport News since 1970, and Dominion Terminal Associates' James River coal pier, owned by Alpha Metallurgical Resources and Arch Resources, has 22 million tons a year of throughput capacity for vessels to 178,000 dwt.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section III and Section V

name: Chesapeake
companies: Perdue AgriBusiness Chesapeake terminal and soybean extraction plant
industrialProfile: Chesapeake's industry runs along the Southern Branch of the Elizabeth River rather than through the suburban city centre. Perdue AgriBusiness operates there what it describes as the largest grain export, import and domestic handling facility on the East Coast, pairing a terminal elevator for corn, wheat, soybeans and barley with a soybean extraction plant producing Hi-Pro meal and crude degummed oil. Kinder Morgan's Elizabeth River Terminal handles fertilizer, scrap steel and bulk, and SeaGate Terminals runs a 44-acre dry and break-bulk berth, all served by the Norfolk and Portsmouth Belt Line to CSX and Norfolk Southern. Inland, Sumitomo Machinery Corporation of America builds Cyclo and Paramax gear drives in about 200,000 square feet on Holland Boulevard.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section V and Section VIII

name: Baltimore
companies: Talen Energy Brandon Shores and H.A. Wagner generating stations
ASR Group Domino Sugar Baltimore refinery, Locust Point
industrialProfile: Baltimore's inspection demand clusters in Curtis Bay and around the harbour. Grace's 110-acre Curtis Bay Works, its largest North American plant, runs ten production units making fluid cracking, hydroprocessing and polyolefin catalysts and silicas with roughly 500 employees, including the world's oldest silica gel plant, operating since 1923. CSX's Curtis Bay coal piers carry about 14 million short tons a year of throughput capacity. Talen Energy's coal-fired Brandon Shores and oil-fired H.A. Wagner units run past their 2025 retirement dates under a FERC-approved reliability-must-run settlement through May 2029. ASR Group's Domino Sugar refinery at Locust Point refines up to 6 million pounds a day and recently added four 160-foot silos.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section I, V and VIII

name: Sparrows Point
companies: Terminal Investment Limited (Sparrows Point Container Terminal)
BAE Systems Titan floating dry dock
Volkswagen Group of America vehicle processing centre
industrialProfile: Sparrows Point is the Baltimore County peninsula where Bethlehem Steel's mill, once the world's largest, closed in 2012; it now trades as Tradepoint Atlantic with roughly 20 tenants including Amazon, Under Armour, Home Depot, FedEx Ground, Floor & Decor and a 150,000-square-foot Volkswagen vehicle processing centre, and about 12,000 people on site. Heavy marine work continues at the Sparrows Point Shipyard, reunified with the property in 2018, where BAE Systems' 950-by-192-foot Titan floating dry dock underwent a five-month repair programme. Tradepoint and Terminal Investment Limited broke ground in May 2026 on a 168-acre container terminal with on-dock rail. US Wind's Sparrows Point Steel monopile plant remains unbuilt after its $47 million federal award was terminated.
localCompliance: ASME BPVC Section V and Section VIII

name: Salina Cruz
companies: PEMEX Refinería Ing. Antonio Dovalí Jaime
Corredor Interoceánico del Istmo de Tehuantepec (CIIT)
industrialProfile: PEMEX's Ing. Antonio Dovalí Jaime refinery, in service since 1979, is the country's largest at 330,000 bpd nominal — roughly 20% of national crude processing capacity. A delayed coker of about US$3 billion is under construction, reported at 76% physical progress in March 2026; it is designed to add 75,000 bpd of low-sulfur gasoline and diesel and cut fuel-oil yield by around 84%. The Pacific port handles PEMEX crude and product movements and is the western terminus of the Interoceanic Corridor of the Isthmus of Tehuantepec, where a container terminal and rail viaduct access have been built. Outside hydrocarbons and the port, the industrial base is genuinely narrow.
localCompliance: NOM-020-STPS-2011 (pressure vessels, cryogenic vessels and boilers)
ASEA SASISOPA safety and environmental management system
ISO 9712 NDT personnel certification (referenced by PEMEX NRFs)
API 510 and API 653 for refinery vessels and storage tanks

name: Minatitlán
industrialProfile: The General Lázaro Cárdenas refinery, built in 1906 and the oldest in Latin America, carries 285,000 bpd of nameplate capacity and was heavily reconfigured with the IMP, ICA Fluor and others. It now runs far below nameplate: crude processing fell to about 50,400 bpd in June 2026, a 58.8% year-on-year drop, so scope skews to turnarounds, coker and hydrotreater rehabilitation and tank work rather than new build. Its slate covers Magna and Premium UBA, Diesel UBA, jet fuel, asphalt, LPG, propylene, coke and elemental sulfur. PEMEX's Cosoleacaque petrochemical complex — 103 hectares and Mexico's only ammonia producer — sits immediately adjacent on the Cosoleacaque–Minatitlán boundary.
localCompliance: ASEA SASISOPA safety and environmental management system
API 510 and API 570 vessel and process piping inspection
ASME BPVC Section V nondestructive examination

name: Coatzacoalcos
companies: Terminal Química Puerto México (Advario / Braskem Idesa)
industrialProfile: Mexico's densest petrochemical cluster. Braskem Idesa's Etileno XXI complex runs an ethane cracker rated 1 million t/y feeding three polyethylene plants with 1.05 million t/y of combined nameplate. The US$500 million Terminal Química Puerto México, an Advario / Braskem Idesa ethane import terminal inaugurated in May 2025 on the Pajaritos lagoon, holds two cryogenic tanks totaling 54,000 tonnes and moves up to 80,000 bpd of ethane through an 11 km pipeline to the cracker. PEMEX's Cangrejera complex, 45 years old in 2026, and the neighbouring Morelos complex are under a rehabilitation programme targeting about 520,000 t/y across five plants. The port is the Gulf terminus of the Interoceanic Corridor.
localCompliance: NOM-020-STPS-2011 (pressure vessels, cryogenic vessels and boilers)
ASEA SASISOPA safety and environmental management system
CRE permits for midstream storage and transport

name: Tula de Allende
companies: CFE Central Termoeléctrica Francisco Pérez Ríos
Cooperativa La Cruz Azul (Tula cement plant)
industrialProfile: The Miguel Hidalgo refinery, in service since 18 March 1976 and spread over 749 hectares with 33 process plants, carries 315,000 bpd of installed capacity and anchors fuel supply to central Mexico. Its long-delayed coker reached 96.2% physical progress at the end of 2025 and entered partial operation, with support plants — steam, hydrogen and reliability tie-ins — integrated during 2026, which is where most current mechanical-integrity scope sits. CFE's Francisco Pérez Ríos station next door runs five 300 MW units historically fired on fuel oil. Cooperativa La Cruz Azul is rebuilding its Tula cement plant with a MXN 6.5 billion investment toward 3 million t/y, restart targeted for November 2026.
localCompliance: ASEA SASISOPA safety and environmental management system
API 510 and API 653 for vessels and storage tanks

name: Salamanca
companies: PEMEX Refinería Ing. Antonio M. Amor (RIAMA)
CFE Central de Ciclo Combinado Salamanca
industrialProfile: The Ing. Antonio M. Amor refinery, opened in 1950 as PEMEX's first self-built plant, covers 518 hectares with roughly 45 process units and about 220,000 bpd of crude capacity, supplying Aguascalientes, Colima, Durango, Guanajuato, Jalisco, Michoacán, Nayarit, San Luis Potosí and Zacatecas; throughput fell sharply during 2026. CFE commissioned a 927 MW combined-cycle station at Salamanca in February 2025, retiring the 1971 fuel-oil plant after 55 years and joining a 393 MW gas-turbine unit from 2015, so HRSG, steam-piping and turbine scope now sits alongside refinery work. Mazda's Salamanca vehicle plant, its first standalone North American site (2014), is rated at 250,000 units a year.
localCompliance: ASEA SASISOPA safety and environmental management system
API 510 and API 653 for vessels and storage tanks
ASME B31.1 power piping for the combined-cycle scope
IATF 16949 for the Mazda supply chain

name: Cadereyta Jiménez
companies: PEMEX Refinería Ing. Héctor R. Lara Sosa
industrialProfile: Cadereyta Jiménez is effectively a one-asset town for inspection work, and the honest read is that the base is narrow rather than diverse. PEMEX's Ing. Héctor R. Lara Sosa refinery, begun in 1973 and inaugurated 18 March 1979, holds roughly 275,000 bpd of crude capacity and is the fuel supply point for Nuevo León, Chihuahua and Coahuila, with partial coverage of Tamaulipas, Durango, San Luis Potosí and Zacatecas. Its slate covers Magna and Diesel UBA, propylene, LPG, sulfur and coke, and the site is credited with supporting more than 20,000 jobs. Beyond the fence line there are product pipelines and terminals, with Monterrey-metro fabrication shops about 40 km west.
localCompliance: ASEA SASISOPA safety and environmental management system

name: Ciudad Madero
industrialProfile: The Francisco I. Madero refinery in Ciudad Madero, founded in 1914 by El Águila and now PEMEX-operated, is rated about 186,000 bpd and was reconfigured to run heavy Maya crude. Yields remain unbalanced — it has produced more fuel oil, around 23,000 bpd, than gasoline at roughly 13,000 bpd. PEMEX opened about 30 tenders at the end of December 2025 covering crude storage tank rehabilitation, butane spheres, specialized maintenance and multi-year supply, aimed at a 2026 operational restart; that tender list reads as an inspection programme in itself — tank bottoms, sphere shells and process piping. The site adjoins the Tampico port and the Pánuco river fabrication yards.
localCompliance: ASEA SASISOPA safety and environmental management system

name: Dos Bocas (Paraíso)
industrialProfile: The Olmeca refinery at Dos Bocas in Paraíso is Mexico's newest and still in a contested ramp-up rather than steady commercial operation. Nameplate is 340,000 bpd. Both crude combination trains ran together for the first time in late December 2025 and early January 2026, touching roughly 320,000 bpd combined, but sustained throughput peaked near 207,000 bpd in January 2026 yielding no more than about 181,000 bpd of finished product, and refining fell 23% in June 2026 after repeated incidents. Cogeneration adjustments, port dispatch constraints, heavy rainfall and mechanical failures in key units drive the shortfall, so commissioning-grade and reliability inspection dominate. The adjacent marine terminal handles crude export.
localCompliance: ASEA SASISOPA safety and environmental management system
ASME BPVC Section VIII Division 1 and Section V

name: Altamira
companies: Alpek Polyester / Petrotemex Altamira PTA and PET
Terminal de LNG de Altamira (Vopak / Enagás)
industrialProfile: The Altamira industrial port complex, operating since June 1985, runs 14 marine terminals across roughly 1,600 acres, moves over 22 million tonnes a year and ranks fourth in Mexico by container throughput. Alpek Polyester's PTA plant on the Tampico–Mante highway accounts for about 34% of the company's global PTA capacity and feeds an adjacent PET resin plant. INEOS Styrolution's 163-hectare site, established in 1994, produces ABS, ASA, SAN, AMSAN, GPPS and SBC at around 380 kilotonnes. Cabot operates three carbon-black units, two of them for reinforcing grades. The Vopak / Enagás LNG regasification terminal — Mexico's first, from August 2006 — plus a newer LNG bunkering facility add cryogenic scope.
localCompliance: NOM-020-STPS-2011 (pressure vessels, cryogenic vessels and boilers)
CRE permits for LNG regasification and storage
API 620 and API 653 for refrigerated and atmospheric tanks

name: Veracruz
industrialProfile: TenarisTamsa, founded in Veracruz in 1954, is the metro's industrial anchor: an electric-arc steel shop fed by scrap and sponge iron, continuous casters and seamless rolling mills producing about 1.23 million tonnes a year with roughly 5,000 employees. Around 70% of output is exported to more than 50 countries and 30% goes to Mexican oil and gas, which makes the city Mexico's centre of gravity for pipe-mill NDT — full-body ultrasonic wall and flaw inspection, electromagnetic testing and end-area examination on OCTG and line pipe. The port is Mexico's third by container volume and the main vehicle gateway, expanding behind a 4.3 km breakwater; Grupo CICE opened a 22-hectare terminal with a 550 m berth in April 2025.
localCompliance: API 5CT and API 5L with their mill NDE requirements
ASTM E213 ultrasonic testing of metal pipe and tubing
ASTM E309 eddy-current examination of steel tubular products

name: Monterrey
companies: Ternium Guerrero plant, San Nicolás de los Garza
industrialProfile: Ternium's Guerrero works at San Nicolás de los Garza — the former Hylsa plant founded in 1942 — runs electric-arc furnace and direct-reduced-iron units. At the company's Pesquería industrial center a 4.4 million t/y hot rolling mill started in mid-2021, and a 2.6 million t/y EAF steel shop with a 2.1 million t/y DRI module is due to commission between late 2026 and early 2027, alongside a 550,000 t/y pickling line, a cold mill and a 1.6 million t/y galvanizing line. Frisa Forjados in Santa Catarina rolls seamless and contoured rings on five radial-axial mills and four hydraulic presses; its Wyman-Gordon joint venture next door forges nickel and titanium aerospace parts. Deacero and Cemex complete the base.
localCompliance: AS9100D and Nadcap for forged aerospace components
IATF 16949 for the automotive supply chain

name: Saltillo
industrialProfile: Saltillo–Ramos Arizpe is a vehicle assembly and powertrain metro — deep rather than broad, with no refining or process-plant base to speak of. Stellantis runs five plants around Saltillo: a Ramos Arizpe engine plant, a south engine plant, stamping, truck assembly and van assembly, building most Ram pickups and ProMaster vans. GM's Ramos Arizpe complex covers engine and transmission assembly, body stamping and vehicle assembly, producing propulsion systems plus the Chevrolet Blazer and Equinox. Daimler's Saltillo truck plant, opened in 2009, employs more than 3,800 people building Freightliner Cascadia Class 8 tractors at roughly 55,000 units a year. John Deere builds front-end loaders and tractor cabs at Ramos Arizpe, with hydraulic, transmission and motor components from Saltillo.
localCompliance: AWS D1.1 and AWS D1.3 sheet steel welding
ASTM E1444 magnetic particle testing and ASTM E1417 liquid penetrant testing

name: Querétaro
companies: Safran (Querétaro engine MRO and Safran Aero Composites)
industrialProfile: Querétaro is Mexico's most balanced aerospace cluster — manufacturing, MRO and engineering rather than assembly alone — with more than 80 aerospace firms and cluster output past US$2.8 billion in 2024. Safran began a US$48 million expansion of Safran Aero Composites in December 2025, adding titanium leading-edge lines for LEAP-1A and LEAP-1B, then inaugurated a US$140 million engine MRO complex in June 2026 sized for up to 350 engine shop visits a year, set to be Safran's largest maintenance centre worldwide. Bombardier builds aviation products, Aernnova makes wings, stabilizers and fuselages, and GE, Airbus and Meggitt are present. Auto parts output reached US$9.327 billion in 2025, fifth in Mexico.
localCompliance: Nadcap accreditation for NDT special processes
ASTM E1417 liquid penetrant testing and ASTM E1444 magnetic particle testing
IATF 16949 for the auto parts supply chain

name: Tampico
companies: PEMEX Refinería Francisco I. Madero (Ciudad Madero)
industrialProfile: Tampico is an offshore fabrication and marine services port rather than a process-plant town. The harbour has 24 berths and carries oil-rig building facilities and drydocks along the south bank of the Pánuco. TMM Astillero, adjacent to the city, works 25 hectares of yard with 500 linear metres of river frontage on a nine-metre canal, and handles floating production unit installation and logistics base services. PEMEX has had six relocatable offshore platforms built at Eseasa facilities in Tamaulipas using around 800 local workers — two permanent structures and four relocatable units with deepwater displacement capacity. Structural weld inspection, jacket and deck fabrication QA dominate. The 186,000 bpd Francisco I. Madero refinery is immediately south in Ciudad Madero.
localCompliance: ASEA SASISOPA safety and environmental management system
API RP 2X ultrasonic and magnetic examination of offshore structural fabrication

name: Ciudad Juárez
industrialProfile: Roughly 300 maquiladora plants operate on the Juárez side of the border; they exported about US$9 billion in the single month of March 2025, up 33% year on year. Bosch, Lear, Aptiv, Foxconn, Honeywell, Yazaki, Electrolux and Schneider Electric all run major operations there, with automotive and auto parts, electronics, medical devices, metal-mechanics, home appliances and logistics as the six leading sectors. Foxconn has put more than US$500 million into Juárez sites including an Nvidia AI-server line, adding US$168 million in 2025. Energy and pipeline scope sits just south of the city: the 907 MW Norte III combined-cycle plant, the 700 MW Samalayuca II CCGT 42 km away, and the Tarahumara gas pipeline running from the border to El Encino.
localCompliance: NOM-007-ASEA-2016 natural gas and ethane pipeline transport

name: Texarkana
industrialProfile: Texarkana's industrial base straddles the state line and is anchored by Red River Army Depot, a 15,375-acre Army depot-level maintenance installation 18 miles west of the city that rebuilds tactical wheeled vehicles alongside the Defense Logistics Agency and its contractor base. The Goodyear-owned former Cooper Tire plant on the Arkansas side builds passenger and light-truck tires with roughly 1,800 employees. Domtar's Ashdown Mill, 30 miles northeast, is one of the world's largest fluff pulp facilities following its 2016 paper-machine conversion and runs its own mill power station. TexAmericas Center redevelops the former Lone Star Army Ammunition Plant. Union Pacific and CPKC meet here, making Texarkana a railcar and interchange town.
localCompliance: ASME Section VIII Div. 1 and Section IX

name: Monroe
companies: Graphic Packaging International West Monroe Mill
industrialProfile: Northeast Louisiana's industrial base is narrow and concentrated in two process plants. Graphic Packaging International's West Monroe mill, operating since 1924, makes food-grade coated recycled paperboard with roughly 800 employees and is unusual in using treated municipal wastewater as mill process water. Fifteen miles north at Sterlington, ANGUS Chemical (Advancion) runs its flagship nitroalkane site, producing more than 40 nitroalkane-derived specialty products for metalworking fluids, coatings, pharmaceuticals and personal care, and completed a TRIS AMINO hydrochloride expansion in 2022. Lumen Technologies keeps its corporate headquarters in Monroe. Beyond those, the workload is shallow Monroe Gas Field gathering, timber and hospital plant — there is no refinery here.

name: Alexandria
companies: DIS-TRAN Steel / DIS-TRAN Packaged Substations (Crest Industries)
industrialProfile: Central Louisiana's inspection work is built around railcar fabrication and utility steel rather than process plant. Union Tank Car's Alexandria works, opened in 2006 on a 122-acre site, builds standard tank car types in high volume, though the company has cut Louisiana production in recent years. In Pineville, Crest Industries' DIS-TRAN Steel fabricates tapered-tubular transmission poles and substation structures and DIS-TRAN Packaged Substations builds high-voltage substations and switchyards. Procter & Gamble's Pineville plant makes Tide and Gain in liquid and unit-dose form with more than 500 employees. Cleco is headquartered in Pineville and runs the Brame Energy Center at Lena, including a carbon capture unit. Hunt Forest Products and Stella-Jones add wood-products plant.
localCompliance: AAR M-1003 quality assurance for tank car builders

name: Pine Bluff
companies: Suzano Pine Bluff Mill (former Pactiv Evergreen)
Union Pacific Pine Bluff yard and locomotive shop
industrialProfile: Pine Bluff Arsenal covers more than 13,500 acres and 660 buildings near White Hall and is the only North American site able to fill white phosphorus munitions; it also makes smoke, illuminating and infrared rounds and fabricates, tests and repairs CBRN masks, filters and protective clothing, having finished incinerating its 3,500-ton chemical agent stockpile in 2010. A $1.3 billion munitions plant has been announced there. Suzano acquired the 800-worker Pine Bluff mill in October 2024 — home of the world's largest gable-top liquid packaging paperboard capacity — and has spent $62 million modernising it. Central Moloney builds distribution transformers on West Sixth Avenue and Jefferson Parkway. Union Pacific runs a hump yard and a reopened locomotive shop.

name: El Dorado
companies: Delek US El Dorado refinery (Lion Oil)
industrialProfile: El Dorado sits on the Smackover brine trend and carries a refining-plus-bromine chemistry load unusual for a town its size. Delek US's El Dorado refinery, the former Lion Oil plant, has 80,000 bpd nameplate crude capacity and is the only refinery in Arkansas, more than 90% of statewide refining capacity, producing fuels, asphalt and solvents. LANXESS runs bromine extraction and derivatives off the Smackover brine field, a business Arkansas has operated since 1957, and hosts Standard Lithium's demonstration plants, producing lithium products since May 2020. LSB Industries operates a 150-acre multi-product ammonia and nitric acid complex on a 1,400-acre El Dorado site with a carbon capture and sequestration project. Murphy USA is headquartered here.

name: Longview
industrialProfile: Longview is one of the densest pulp-and-paper clusters on the West Coast, and the Washington port and mill town, not Longview, Texas. Smurfit Westrock's Longview kraft mill runs about 1,000 employees, roughly 3,600 tons a day of paper and corrugated grades and 2,800 tons a day of unbleached pulp. NORPAC, the former newsprint mill now making about a million tons of containerboard a year, is being acquired by International Paper. Nippon Dynawave Packaging, making liquid packaging board on site since 1953, has been shut down since 26 May 2026, when a 900,000-gallon white liquor tank collapsed and killed eleven workers; wall thinning had been detected in July 2025. Weyerhaeuser, the Port of Longview and contractor J.H. Kelly complete the base.
localCompliance: WAC 296-104 Washington boiler and unfired pressure vessel rules

name: Kalama
industrialProfile: Kalama is a small Columbia River port town whose industrial base is essentially the Port of Kalama's tenant list — about 1,400 jobs across deep-draft river frontage, with no refinery and no heavy process plant. Steelscape's Kalama works metallic-coats and paints steel coil for the construction market with around 260 employees and is the main coating-line and process asset in town. TEMCO, the CHS and Cargill joint venture, runs the Kalama Export Terminal, handling up to 250 million bushels a year of feed grains, oilseeds and wheat for Asia-Pacific markets and loading as much as 2 million bushels in 24 hours with roughly 120 workers; a federally funded rail expansion is underway. Smaller tenants make wine bottles, aerospace parts, food packaging and lumber.
localCompliance: WAC 296-104 Washington boiler and unfired pressure vessel rules

name: Vancouver
companies: United Grain Corporation Vancouver Export Terminal
industrialProfile: Clark County holds about two-thirds of Washington's semiconductor manufacturing employment, and Vancouver is its centre. SEH America, Shin-Etsu Handotai's US arm, makes silicon wafers here with roughly 680 to 865 workers; WaferTech and HP each run around 1,000; nLight builds diode lasers and fibre components. On the river, United Grain Corporation's Vancouver Export Terminal is the largest grain export terminal on the US West Coast at up to six million tonnes a year, and the Port of Vancouver USA also handles wind components and bulk cargo. Great Western Malting has malted in Vancouver since 1934 with 340,000 tonnes of annual capacity. Farwest Steel runs a 330,000 sq ft service centre, and BPA's Ross Complex is its largest industrial service hub.
localCompliance: WAC 296-104 Washington boiler and unfired pressure vessel rules

name: Everett
industrialProfile: Everett is Boeing's widebody town. The Everett plant, the largest building in the world by volume, assembles the 767 and KC-46A and the 777 and 777X, and since 6 July 2026 also runs a new $1 billion 737 MAX North Line — the first 737 final assembly outside Renton. The Port of Everett is Washington's second-largest port by economic output and moves the largest aerospace components for the 767, 777, 777X and KC-46 programmes by sea, rail and heavy haul; its 40-acre Norton Terminal, built on the remediated Kimberly-Clark mill site, opened in 2022. Naval Station Everett homeports seven guided-missile destroyers plus Coast Guard and Military Sealift Command vessels. Fluke Corporation designs and manufactures test instruments here.
localCompliance: WAC 296-104 Washington boiler and unfired pressure vessel rules

name: Bremerton
companies: Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility
Naval Undersea Warfare Center Division Keyport
industrialProfile: Bremerton is a one-employer industrial town and that employer is nuclear. Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility employs roughly 15,000 civilians and is the Navy's primary provider of maintenance, repair, modernisation, inactivation and recycling for Pacific Fleet ships, submarines and aircraft carriers. It is the only Navy shipyard on the West Coast with a dry dock able to take a nuclear-powered aircraft carrier, and the only Navy shipyard approved to recycle nuclear-powered submarines. The Navy has advanced a roughly $30 billion Bremerton waterfront programme, including a new dry dock sized for its largest carriers, with a draft EIS issued in July 2025 and construction targeted for spring 2028. Bangor's Trident submarine base and NUWC Keyport round out Kitsap County.
localCompliance: NAVSEA S9074-AR-GIB-010/278 welding and brazing requirements
NAVSEA 0900-LP-001-7000 fabrication and inspection of ship structure
WAC 296-104 Washington boiler and unfired pressure vessel rules

name: Port Angeles
industrialProfile: Port Angeles's base narrowed sharply when McKinley Paper permanently closed its containerboard mill in 2024, laying off about 190 workers five years after converting the former newsprint machine to 100% recycled fibre; management said it hoped to idle rather than scrap the plant. What is left is marine trades. Platypus Marine runs one of the Pacific Northwest's largest indoor full-service shipyards on ten acres of harbour frontage with 1,000 feet of deep-water dock and 35-foot draft haul-out, doing refit, repair and new construction and subcontracting for yacht builders including Westport. The Port of Port Angeles operates the Port Angeles Boat Yard, Terminal 1 and an 18-acre Marine Trades Industrial Park built on a former mill site, plus log export.
localCompliance: ABS Rules for Building and Classing Marine Vessels
USCG 46 CFR Subchapter T small passenger vessel inspection
WAC 296-104 Washington boiler and unfired pressure vessel rules

name: Coos Bay
companies: Oregon International Port of Coos Bay
Roseburg Forest Products chip export terminal
Pacific Coast Intermodal Port / NorthPoint Development
industrialProfile: Coos Bay is Oregon's only deep-draft coastal harbour and its industry is port, rail and wood — a genuinely narrow base since Georgia-Pacific closed its sawmill permanently in 2019, taking 111 jobs. The Oregon International Port of Coos Bay moves roughly two million tons of cargo a year across terminals on the North Spit, East Bay, Upper Bay and Charleston, owns and operates the Coos Bay Rail Line connecting to Union Pacific at Eugene, and handles over 25 million pounds of seafood a year through Charleston Marina, which includes a shipyard and dry storage. Roseburg Forest Products ships wood chips to Japan from its export terminal. The Pacific Coast Intermodal Port, with NorthPoint Development and $100 million in state bonding, would add container capacity up to 2 million TEU.
localCompliance: ABS Rules for Building and Classing Marine Vessels
OAR 918-225 Oregon boiler and pressure vessel rules

name: Astoria
companies: Hyak Maritime Tongue Point / WCT Marine & Construction
industrialProfile: Astoria's base is seafood and small-vessel marine work, plus one large paper mill just upriver. Bornstein Seafoods has moved its headquarters to Astoria and runs about 150 year-round staff and up to 300 in season; Da Yang Seafood processes here as well, and their joint venture with Scoular opened a $17.5 million fishmeal plant at the Port of Astoria's Warrenton airport industrial park in 2023. At Tongue Point, Hyak Maritime's shipyard hosts WCT Marine & Construction and Bergerson Construction, though tenants sued in 2026 and the yard's electric travel lift has seen almost no use. Hampton Lumber's Warrenton mill employs about 140 and chips to Georgia-Pacific's Wauna mill at Clatskanie, which runs five tissue machines and roughly 850 workers.
localCompliance: USCG 46 CFR Subchapter C uninspected commercial fishing vessel requirements
ABS Rules for Building and Classing Marine Vessels
OAR 918-225 Oregon boiler and pressure vessel rules

name: Eureka
companies: Humboldt Bay Independent Spent Fuel Storage Installation
Humboldt Redwood Company Scotia mill and biomass plant
Humboldt Bay Harbor District offshore wind terminal
industrialProfile: Humboldt Bay's industrial load is power plant, biomass and a nuclear legacy site, with an offshore wind terminal in build-out. PG&E's Humboldt Bay Generating Station is 163 MW from ten dual-fuel Wärtsilä 18V50DF reciprocating engine-generator sets of 16.3 MW each, certified in 2008 and commercial from October 2012. Beside it sits the Humboldt Bay ISFSI holding spent fuel from Unit 3, shut down in 1976 — the reactor is decommissioned but the cask pad remains, and sea-level rise is an acknowledged concern. DG Fairhaven's 17.25 MW biomass plant runs on the Samoa Peninsula, and Humboldt Redwood Company's 32.5 MW Scotia plant burns residue from its adjacent sawmill and planer mill. The Harbor District's 180-acre heavy-lift offshore wind terminal is the growth item.
localCompliance: California Title 8 Pressure Vessel Safety Orders (Cal/OSHA)
10 CFR Part 72 independent spent fuel storage licensing

name: Decatur, Alabama
industrialProfile: Decatur's plants line Wheeler Lake on the Tennessee River in one of the South's densest chemical-and-metals clusters. Nucor Steel Decatur runs an electric-arc flat-rolled sheet mill, with a new $125 million Nucor Towers & Structures plant at Mallard-Fox Creek making steel transmission poles. Ascend Performance Materials has produced adiponitrile for nylon 6,6 here for over 60 years; Indorama Ventures runs paraxylene and PTA units; Daikin America makes fluorochemicals. Toray Composite Materials America has run precursor-through-carbon-fiber lines since 1997 and recently doubled TORAYCA T1100 aerospace-grade capacity. 3M's 2.5-million-square-foot materials and film site employs about 788. TVA's three-unit Browns Ferry boiling-water reactor station sits across the lake.
localCompliance: ASME Section XI (Browns Ferry in-service inspection)

name: Muscle Shoals
industrialProfile: The Shoals base is narrow and one plant carries it. Constellium Muscle Shoals is an aluminium rolling complex of roughly 1,250 people with more than 100 acres under roof - five casting units, hot and cold rolling mills, and a slitting and finishing centre - turning out over a billion pounds a year of finished coil, including can body, end and tab stock. The site was built as Reynolds in 1941 for wartime aircraft sheet and ran as Wise Alloys before Constellium. Around it: TVA's Wilson Dam and Muscle Shoals Reservation, the retired Colbert coal units and their gas turbines, Cherokee Nitrogen's chemical plant and Essity's tissue mill in Colbert County.

name: Calvert City
industrialProfile: Calvert City is a compact chemical enclave on the Tennessee River above the Ohio confluence in Marshall County. Westlake's 550-acre complex is fully integrated: an ethylene cracker rated around 450 million pounds a year, chlor-alkali at roughly 550 million pounds of chlorine and 605 million pounds of caustic soda, plus EDC, VCM and PVC units - a 2016 mechanical failure on the ethylene unit took the entire complex down, which shows how tightly coupled it is. Arkema has operated here since 1949, making Kynar PVDF and Forane refrigerants including R-32 and 1233zd. Wacker makes polymer binders, Ashland's ISP Chemicals runs specialty units, and Air Products holds a site. Barge docks and rail serve all of it.

name: Owensboro
industrialProfile: Owensboro's work is metal fabrication and consumer-goods converting rather than heavy process. Metalsa stamps and welds truck frames and builds every Jeep Gladiator structural frame; Toyotetsu Mid-America presses and welds automotive body components with over 500 employees; Kimberly-Clark converts tissue and personal-care products; Swedish Match makes ZYN nicotine pouches, the only US site producing that line; Specialty Foods Group runs a large meat plant. Other automotive suppliers include Daicel Safety Systems, Daramic, OMICO and Ritatsu. The heavier assets are upriver in Hancock County - the Commonwealth Rolled Products Lewisport aluminium mill with over 1,000 employees, and the idled Century Aluminum Hawesville smelter, bought in 2026 by a data-centre developer.

name: Henderson, Kentucky
industrialProfile: Henderson County is metals and generation. Century Aluminum's Sebree smelter at Robards, built in 1973 and bought by Century in 2013, is one of the few primary aluminium smelters still running in the United States - roughly 205,000 to 220,000 tonnes a year of hot metal, about 625 workers, with USW Local 9443-00 under contract through 2028. Accuride makes heavy steel truck wheels; Gibbs Die Casting, a Koch Enterprises company, runs high-pressure aluminium die casting; Audubon Metals is the only combined heavy-media separator and secondary specification aluminium alloy producer under one roof in the country, at 332 employees. Big Rivers Electric is headquartered in Henderson and runs coal units near Sebree.

name: Evansville
industrialProfile: Evansville anchors a tri-state stretch of the Ohio River. Kaiser Aluminum's Warrick rolling mill at Newburgh is one of only four dedicated can-sheet mills in North America, with about 1,170 employees; the co-located Alcoa smelter closed permanently in 2023, leaving the mill as the site's anchor. Downriver at Mount Vernon, SABIC operates its largest manufacturing complex in North America. Toyota Motor Manufacturing Indiana at Princeton represents roughly $8 billion of cumulative investment and is adding a battery-electric SUV under a $1.4 billion programme announced in 2024. Berry Global is headquartered in Evansville. AEP's two-unit Rockport coal station and Cleveland-Cliffs' Rockport Works finishing lines sit on the Indiana bank.
localCompliance: Indiana Boiler and Pressure Vessel Rules (675 IAC)

name: Terre Haute
industrialProfile: Terre Haute runs on film, packaging and automotive components, with one large process plant arriving. Amcor's former Bemis operation is the biggest manufacturer at about 679 people making polyethylene bags and flexible packaging, and Taghleef Industries runs oriented polypropylene film lines at roughly 420. Great Dane builds truck trailers with about 451; ADVICS machines brake components at 539; thyssenkrupp Presta makes steering components and GE Aviation machines turbine engine parts, each around 430. The heavy-process anchor is Wabash Valley Resources at West Terre Haute, converting the shuttered Wabash River coal-gasification site into a 500,000-ton-a-year low-carbon ammonia plant capturing 1.67 million tons of CO2, on a $1.6 billion DOE loan closed in October 2025.

name: Lima, Ohio
industrialProfile: Lima is a refinery town with the Army's heavy-armour plant attached. The Cenovus Lima Refinery processes about 183,000 barrels a day of heavy, light and synthetic crude into ultra-low-sulphur diesel, low-sulphur gasoline, jet fuel and petrochemical feedstock, inside a $1.5 billion five-year Ohio refining programme. Adjacent to it, INEOS Nitriles makes acrylonitrile and Nutrien runs a large nitrogen complex producing ammonia and downstream nitrogen products. The government-owned, General Dynamics-operated Joint Systems Manufacturing Center - the former Lima Army Tank Plant - has built more than 7,000 M1 Abrams and is the only US plant doing that work. Ford's Lima Engine Plant runs EcoBoost and Duratec V6 lines with roughly 1,394 employees.

name: Marietta, Ohio
industrialProfile: Five plants strung along Ohio Route 7 in Washington County are Marietta's manufacturing base, and three of them descend from a single Union Carbide site. Eramet Marietta melts manganese ferroalloys for North American steelmakers in electric arc furnaces running near 3,000 degrees F, with about 180 employees. Kraton Polymers, opened in 1961 as a Shell Chemical plant, makes styrenic block copolymers and polyisoprene latex with roughly 400 direct staff and up to 600 including contractors. Solvay Specialty Polymers, bought from BP Amoco in 2001, makes sulfone polymers for medical and dental instruments and water-filtration membranes with 310 people. Americas Styrenics runs polystyrene, and Orion Engineered Carbons has made carbon black here since 1968.

name: Parkersburg
industrialProfile: Parkersburg's industry is fluoropolymers. Chemours' Washington Works, seven miles down the Ohio in Wood County, is the company's largest advanced performance materials site - 1,250 company-owned acres opened by DuPont in 1948, making Teflon PTFE and PFA and related fluoroproducts for semiconductor, automotive, aerospace and construction markets, with a PFA capacity expansion announced. It is a multi-tenant complex: Kuraray America joined in 2014 with safety-glass, architectural and automotive materials, and Celanese also operates on site. Downriver at Ravenswood, Constellium runs one of the world's largest rolled-plate operations, with the most powerful plate stretchers in the world. Upriver at Willow Island, the Pleasants Power Station's hydrogen conversion collapsed into Chapter 11 in July 2026.
localCompliance: West Virginia Boiler Safety Act (WV Code 21-3)

name: Weirton
industrialProfile: Weirton has changed hands. Cleveland-Cliffs Weirton, the last operating remnant of Weirton Steel and historically about 300,000 net tons a year of tin mill products, was indefinitely idled in April 2024 after an adverse ITC ruling on tin mill imports, cutting roughly 900 jobs; the electrical-transformer plant meant to replace it was later cancelled. What did land is Form Energy's Form Factory 1 on the former Weirton Steel land - a 550,000-square-foot plant built in about a year, now in commercial production of 100-hour iron-air batteries with nearly 400 employees, scaling toward 850,000 square feet and at least 500 MW a year by 2028. Pietro Fiorentini USA builds natural-gas pressure regulators and metering systems at Three Springs.
localCompliance: ASME B31.8 (gas transmission and distribution piping)

name: Wheeling
industrialProfile: Wheeling itself is a services, healthcare and back-office town; the heavy industry sits downriver in Marshall and Wetzel counties and is driven by Marcellus and Utica gas. Blue Racer Midstream's Natrium complex, a two-mile-long plant on the Ohio River about twelve miles south of Moundsville, processes 400 million cubic feet a day and fractionates NGLs. Five miles north of New Martinsville, Westlake's Natrium plant makes chlorine and caustic soda - the acquisition that made Westlake the third-largest US chlor-alkali producer and second-largest PVC producer. AEP's Mitchell coal station generates at Moundsville alongside the retired Kammer units. The ethane cracker long proposed for Belmont County across the river was never built.

name: Steubenville
industrialProfile: Steubenville is the Ohio bank of a steel valley that thinned but did not empty. JSW Steel USA Ohio at Mingo Junction - the 1872 Wheeling-Pittsburgh works - restarted its electric arc furnace in December 2018 after 3,545 days cold, melting scrap to slab and hot-rolled coil, with more than $119 million committed to plant and equipment. Downriver at Brilliant, the 1.8-gigawatt three-unit Cardinal plant runs under Buckeye Power and drew $34 million of federal life-extension funding for Units 1 and 2 in February 2026. Across the river at Follansbee, Wheeling-Nippon Steel makes all five major hot-dip coated products including Zn-Al-Mg; Cliffs' Mountain State Carbon coke batteries there shut in 2022.
localCompliance: ASTM A388 (ultrasonic examination of steel forgings)

name: Ashtabula
industrialProfile: Ashtabula pairs a Lake Erie bulk port with a chloride-route pigment district. INEOS Pigments runs the two-plant Ashtabula Complex, roughly 245,000 tonnes a year of chloride-process titanium dioxide plus titanium chemicals, making it one of North America's largest TiO2 producers and the leading US producer of titanium chemicals. Its chlorine comes from ASHTA Chemicals next door, a roughly 110-person membrane-cell chlor-alkali unit that also makes potassium hydroxide and potassium carbonate for liquid fertilisers, runway de-icers, food and pharmaceutical use. Molded Fiber Glass, founded in Ashtabula in 1948, moulds composites for wind, heavy truck, defence and water treatment. Pinney Dock, a deep-water NS and CSX transload, moves iron ore, aggregates, sulphur and fertiliser.

name: Painesville
industrialProfile: Painesville sits in Lake County's chemical corridor. Lubrizol's Painesville plant is a 158-acre, roughly 350-employee site making specialty additive systems for lubricating oils, industrial fluids, fuel additives, process chemicals and coating additives, run from the Berkshire Hathaway-owned company's Wickliffe headquarters. Avery Dennison Performance Tapes casts vinyl film and makes specialty papers and labels here and is adding about 32,000 square feet. Mar-Bal moulds thermoset compounds with roughly 200 people, and AeroControlex builds control valves, pumps and assemblies for aerospace, marine and nuclear service. Nine miles east on the Lake Erie shore, Vistra's Perry station operates a single 1,260 MW General Electric boiling water reactor.

name: Duluth
industrialProfile: Duluth is the Great Lakes' iron-ore gateway. Nearly all Mesabi Range taconite moves by rail to the Port of Duluth-Superior, where iron ore is the leading cargo by tonnage and the taconite float has topped 20 million short tons in recent seasons. Cirrus Aircraft, the city's largest manufacturer at roughly 1,200 employees, builds SR-series composite airframes and the Vision Jet at Duluth International, and bought the former AAR maintenance hangar to expand. ME Global casts grinding media and mill liners for the mining industry, Bendtec induction-bends large-diameter pipe, and Altec and IPS Cranes build lift equipment. The work here is docks, rail, mining equipment and airframes rather than process plants.

name: Superior
industrialProfile: Superior carries Wisconsin's only oil refinery.
